definition_zh: 无双的；空前的；无可匹敌的；前所未有的
definition_en: so great or unusual that nothing else can be compared with it as an equal
core_image: 一张地图上找不到第二根与它并行的线，它独自延伸到天边
scene: 经济学家翻出各国家庭负债的百年统计，指着其中一条曲线说，这样的增幅在历史上从未出现。Comparing a century of household debt data, the economist found an unparalleled rise in borrowing.
sceneCN: 这里 unparalleled 是「空前的」（第 2 个义项：程度或规模超过以往一切同类事物）；句意：对比一个世纪的家庭负债数据，这位经济学家发现借贷出现了空前的增长。

pos.zh: 无双的；空前的；无可匹敌的；前所未有的

collocations.zh: 接触某物的便利程度前所未有

derivatives.zh: 平行的；类似的，unparalleled 正是由它加否定前缀 un- 构成
无平行的；不并行的，un- 加 parallel 的另一种较简短构词
平行；对称；并行的性质，parallel 加名词后缀 -ism 构成
无双；独一无二，unparalleled 加名词后缀 -ness 构成的罕见派生词

senses.title: Having no equal in quality
senses.definition: better than anyone or anything else of the same kind, so that no equal can be found
senses.definitionCN: 在同一类中好过任何其他对象，找不到能与之比肩者
senses.example: Her command of the old dialect was unparalleled among modern scholars.
senses.exampleCN: 在现代学者中，她对这种古老方言的掌握无人能及。
senses.why: Parallel first meant a line running alongside another; un- cancels that, so unparalleled describes something no second thing can be placed beside.
senses.whyCN: parallel 原本指与另一条线并行的线，un- 把这种「并行」取消掉，unparalleled 便形容找不出第二条线能与它并肩摆放的事物。

senses.title: Unpreceded in degree or scale
senses.definition: greater in size, speed, or degree than anything of the kind that has happened before
senses.definitionCN: 在规模、速度或程度上超过以往发生的任何同类事物
senses.example: The city saw unparalleled growth in the decade after the railway opened.
senses.exampleCN: 铁路通车后的十年里，这座城市出现了空前的增长。
senses.why: Once nothing can run alongside a thing, it also has no earlier record to stand next to, so the word slides into the sense of unprecedented.
senses.whyCN: 一旦没有东西能与某事物并列，它在历史上也没有可并列的记录，于是词义顺滑地滑向「没有先例」，与 unprecedented 彼此重叠。

senses.title: Beyond comparison in emotion or beauty
senses.definition: so beautiful or moving that any comparison seems inadequate
senses.definitionCN: 美得或动人心魄到任何比较都显得苍白
senses.example: Travelers write of the unparalleled calm of that mountain lake.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行者写到那座高山湖泊无与伦比的宁静。
senses.why: Praise works by removing the standard of measurement; if comparison fails, the feeling is described as unparalleled.
senses.whyCN: 赞美的逻辑是抽掉衡量标准：当比较本身失效时，感受就被称为无与伦比。

senses.title: Lacking a line that runs alongside
senses.definition: used in technical writing for a layout or route that has no line running alongside it
senses.definitionCN: 在技术写作中指布局或路线旁没有与之并行的另一条线
senses.example: The second tunnel was left unparalleled for almost a mile.
senses.exampleCN: 第二条隧道在将近一英里内没有并行的通道。
senses.why: This literal use keeps the geometric image intact; it is rare and largely technical but still takes the un- plus parallel shape.
senses.whyCN: 这一字面用法保留了原来的几何意象：没有与它平行的一条线。它少见且偏技术性，但仍是 un- 加 parallel 的直接组合。

intro.en: Unparalleled is English rather than Latin: the negative prefix un- is added to parallel, which came through French from Latin and ultimately from Greek parallelos, running alongside.
intro.cn: unparalleled 是英语自身的构词，而非拉丁语词：否定前缀 un- 加在 parallel 之上；parallel 经法语、拉丁语上溯，源头是希腊语 parallelos（并排跑）。

items.en: Greek parallelos combines para with allelos, thought to mean one another, so the lines keep the same distance as they run.
items.cn: 希腊语 parallelos 由 para（在旁）与 allelos（彼此）组成，形容两条线保持同样距离延伸。

items.en: Latin borrowing gives parallelos alongside its own caterva-based word paracellus, a close and partly puzzling form.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入 parallelos，同时还有源自 caterva 的写法 paracellus，词形相近，来源关系仍有争议。

items.en: French shortens the term to parallele and applies it to lines and then to persons on a common footing.
items.cn: 法语把词形缩短为 parallele，先用于线条，再引申指地位相仿的人。

items.en: Parallel becomes an adjective and a noun for geometry, and also for a person or case equal to another.
items.cn: parallel 进入英语后成为几何上的形容词与名词，也用来指地位相当的人或类似的情形。

items.en: First found in the late 1590s, un- plus parallel begins with the literal sense of having no line running alongside.
items.cn: un- 加 parallel 的写法首见于十六世纪九十年代末，最初是「没有并行之线」的字面义。

items.en: The literal sense recedes, and unparalleled becomes a strong word of praise for quality, scale, and beauty.
items.cn: 字面义逐渐退居一旁，unparalleled 变成赞美品质、规模与美感的有力词。

note.en: Unparalleled belongs to the parallel family of geometry words, and stands close to adjectives of being the best without equal.
note.cn: unparalleled 属于以 parallel 为代表的几何词族，同时与「无人能及」的一类形容词相邻。

entries.definition: lying in the same direction and always the same distance apart
entries.definitionCN: parallel 指方向相同、距离始终不变的平行；unparalleled 就是给它加上否定前缀

entries.definition: a four-sided shape whose opposite sides are parallel
entries.definitionCN: 平行四边形，与 parallel 同源，都用「平行」这一几何意象

entries.definition: the state of being parallel or similarly shaped
entries.definitionCN: 平行、对称的性质；由 parallel 加 -ism 构成

entries.definition: not affected by paralysis
entries.definitionCN: 只是拼写相近：词根是 paralyse（瘫痪），与「平行」无关，词源不同

entries.definition: better than everyone else and having no equal
entries.definitionCN: 无人能及的，英式拼写；美式写作 unequaled，强调没有对等者

entries.definition: never having happened before
entries.definitionCN: 前所未有的，着眼点在时间上的「从未发生过」

entries.definition: having no equal among its kind
entries.definitionCN: 无双的，语气偏文学，多用于赞美人物与作品

normalIntro.en: Unparalleled is un- plus parallel: take away the negative prefix and you have the word for lines that run side by side.
normalIntro.cn: unparalleled 就是 un- 加 parallel：去掉否定前缀，剩下的是「并排延伸」的那个词。

normal.en: Un- is the negative prefix of unhappy and unfair, so unparalleled means no parallel at all.
normal.cn: un- 是否定前缀，如 unhappy 与 unfair，所以 unparalleled 就是「完全没有平行」的意思。

normal.en: Parallel lines never meet, which gives the picture of two things running side by side.
normal.cn: 平行线永不交汇，这给了我们两样东西并排延伸的画面。

normal.en: In collocations unparalleled usually comes before the noun, as in unparalleled success.
normal.cn: 在搭配中 unparalleled 通常放在名词之前，如 unparalleled success。

normal.en: Do not write the word as two separate pieces; it is one adjective spelled with a double l near the end.
normal.cn: 不要把它拆成两截写，这是一个整体形容词，词尾附近有双写的 l。

normal.en: For a factual record use unprecedented, and keep unparalleled for the stronger note of praise.
normal.cn: 陈述客观记录时多用 unprecedented，unparalleled 更适合更强的赞美意味。

abstract.en: Picture two rails lying side by side, until one of them simply has nothing to lie beside.
abstract.cn: 想象两条并肩的铁轨，后来其中一条忽然找不到可以并排的伙伴。（对应第 1 个义项：找不到对等者）

abstract.en: See a rising graph whose line runs so high that earlier years have no line to trace beside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一张上升的曲线图，线冲得太高，以前的年份都找不出可对照的线。（对应第 2 个义项：规模空前）

abstract.en: Stand at a mirror held to a lake and find no second picture that could match the first.
abstract.cn: 站在对着湖面的镜子前，却找不到第二幅能与它相配的画面。（对应第 3 个义项：无与伦比的美与感受）

examples.en: The online course gave students unparalleled access to working chemists.
examples.cn: 这门在线课程让学生们获得了接触在职化学家的空前便利。

examples.en: Unparalleled rainfall closed every road into the valley.
examples.cn: 前所未有的降雨封闭了通往山谷的所有道路。

examples.en: The band described the farewell concert as an unparalleled emotional experience.
examples.cn: 乐队把这场告别演出形容为一次无与伦比的情感体验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安帕拉雷欧」——安安静静、别人都追不上，只剩下他一个人在跑，就是无双的。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 希腊语 parallelos（para 在旁 + allelos 彼此，指并排延伸的线）→ 拉丁语 parallelos → 古法语 parallele → 英语 parallel（平行的；类似的）→ un- + parallel → unparalleled，核心义「找不到可与之并行的第二条线」。

sensesIntro.en: Unparalleled always denies a comparison: it starts with quality that has no equal, then reaches scale without precedent, then the beauty that defeats comparison, and finally keeps a rare literal, geometric sense.
sensesIntro.cn: unparalleled 的核心始终是「拒绝比较」：先用于无人能及的质量，再指史无前例的规模，接着是令比较失效的美，最后保留了一个少见而字面的几何义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a single line running on with nothing able to run alongside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条独自延伸的线，旁边找不到能与它并排的另一条线。

branches.en: The quality branch: no rival reaches the same standard.
branches.cn: 品质分支：没有谁能达到同样标准的「无双」。

branches.en: The scale branch: even history offers no line to lay alongside.
branches.cn: 规模分支：连历史里也找不到可以并列的一条线，即「空前」。

branches.en: The aesthetic branch: comparison itself collapses into praise.
branches.cn: 审美分支：比较直接失效，只剩下赞美。

branches.en: The literal branch keeps the geometric picture of parallel lines.
branches.cn: 字面分支保留平行线的几何画面。

branches.en: Both branches live on the same geometry; one draws it, the other only feels it.
branches.cn: 两个分支共用同一套几何骨架：一个真的把线画出来，另一个只在感受里体认。

intro.en: Unparalleled is built with the native negative prefix un- on the borrowed word parallel, and the parallel family supplies practical words such as parallelism and parallelogram.
intro.cn: unparalleled 用英语本族语的否定前缀 un- 加在外来词 parallel 上，parallel 词族还提供 parallelism、parallelogram 等实用构词。

latinIntro.en: The prefix un- is Germanic, not Latin; parallel itself is Greek by way of Latin. The Latin items below are given as semantic parallels, not as ancestors of un-.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 un- 属日耳曼语，不来自拉丁语；parallel 本身是经拉丁语借入的希腊词。下面列出拉丁词只作语义对照，并非 un- 的祖先。

items.example: The prefix un- turns parallel into unparalleled.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 parallel 变成 unparalleled。

items.meaning: lines running side by side, or something closely similar
items.meaningCN: 平行的；可类比的；平行线
items.example: Parallel supplies the idea of two lines side by side.
items.exampleCN: parallel 提供两条线并排的意象。

items.example: Unparalleled nearly always modifies a noun.
items.exampleCN: unparalleled 几乎总是修饰名词。

items.example: The suffix -ism forms parallelism from parallel.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ism 把 parallel 变成 parallelism。

items.meaning: a shape with parallel opposite sides
items.example: The element -gram relates to lines drawn on a page.
items.exampleCN: 构词成分 -gram 与纸上画出的线条有关。

items.example: Unparallel is the shorter un- form but is much rarer.
items.exampleCN: unparallel 是更短的 un- 形式，但远不常用。

items.example: Unprecedented shares the same negative prefix and the sense of no earlier match.
items.exampleCN: unprecedented 使用同样的否定前缀，也表达「没有更早的对应物」。

items.example: Unequalled is its nearest everyday synonym.
items.exampleCN: unequalled 是它最接近的日常同义词。

items.example: The suffix -ly makes the adverb parallelly.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ly 构成副词 parallelly。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 均等的；相等的（仅作语义对照）

definition_zh: 无偏见的；公正的；未受先入之见影响的
definition_en: free from prejudice, so that judgement is not coloured by a fixed opinion formed in advance
core_image: 一副取下的有色眼镜，世界第一次显出原来的颜色
scene: 法庭换了新的陪审员，法官要求在听取双方全部证据之前，每人先闭上眼睛，把先前的猜想清空。Before hearing all the evidence, each juror was asked to keep an unprejudiced mind.
sceneCN: 这里 unprejudiced 是「无偏见的」（第 5 个义项：程序上要求的无成见状态）；句意：在听取全部证据之前，每位陪审员都被要求保持无偏见的头脑。

pos.zh: 无偏见的；公正的；未受先入之见影响的

collocations.zh: 不带先入之见地对待某事

derivatives.zh: 偏见；成见，unprejudiced 即由此加否定前缀 un- 构成
有偏见的；有成见的，正是 unprejudiced 的对立面
无偏见地；公正地，加副词后缀 -ly 构成的罕见词
无偏见；公正，加名词后缀 -ness 构成的罕见派生词

senses.title: Free from bias in judgement
senses.definition: having no fixed opinion in favour of or against someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 不预先偏向或反对某人某事，没有固定的成见
senses.example: A good umpire must stay unprejudiced in every disputed call.
senses.exampleCN: 优秀的裁判在每一次有争议的判罚中都必须保持无偏见。
senses.why: Prejudice is a judgement made in advance, literally a pre-judging; adding un- simply removes that prior verdict from the mind.
senses.whyCN: prejudice 字面就是「预先判断」，即在看清事实之前先下结论；加上 un-，等于把这道提前下好的裁决从心里撤掉。

senses.title: Open to contrary evidence
senses.titleCN: 不持成见的；愿意接受新证据的
senses.definition: willing to consider facts or opinions that differ from what one already believes
senses.definitionCN: 愿意考虑与自己原有看法不同的事实或意见
senses.example: She reads critics of her own field with an unprejudiced curiosity.
senses.exampleCN: 她以无成见的好奇心阅读那些批评自己领域的文章。
senses.why: To be free of prejudice is also to leave room for surprise, so the word describes an attitude rather than a single decision.
senses.whyCN: 摆脱偏见同时也意味着给意外留下空间，因此这个词描写的是一种态度，而不只是一次决断。

senses.title: Unbiased by nationality or social group
senses.titleCN: 不带种族、地域或阶层偏见的
senses.definition: treating people fairly whatever their race, nationality, sex, or social background
senses.definitionCN: 不因种族、国籍、性别或社会出身而区别对待他人
senses.example: Unprejudiced hiring means judging only skills and experience.
senses.exampleCN: 不带偏见的招聘只依据技能与经验作出判断。
senses.why: Modern prejudice is most often social, so the plain un- form frequently answers the word discrimination without naming it.
senses.whyCN: 现代语境中的 prejudice 多指社会性的歧视，因此这个朴素的否定形式常常就是在回应 discrimination，只是不明说。

senses.title: Not distorted by personal interest
senses.titleCN: 未被先入之见扭曲的；未受私利影响的
senses.definition: used of a view or account that is not warped by a personal stake or a prior theory
senses.definitionCN: 用于见解或陈述，指没有被私利或既有理论扭曲
senses.example: The book gives an unprejudiced account of the trade dispute.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书对这场贸易争端给出了不受私利扭曲的叙述。
senses.why: Century Dictionary records a related sense of judgement not warped by prejudice; here the word shifts from the person to the judgement itself.
senses.whyCN: 老词典已收录「判断未被偏见扭曲」的义项：这里词的落点从人身上移到判断本身，用来形容见解是否被私利带偏。

senses.title: Open state of mind required by a procedure
senses.titleCN: 程序要求的无成见状态
senses.definition: the condition of having set aside a prior view, as a court or inquiry demands of a juror or examiner
senses.definitionCN: 搁置原有看法后所处的状态，如法庭对陪审员或调查者对审查者的要求
senses.example: Every candidate was briefed to appear unprejudiced during the review.
senses.exampleCN: 每位候选人都被告知在评审期间须表现出无成见。
senses.why: Institutions regularise the sense: an unprejudiced mind becomes a procedural requirement that can be checked and challenged.
senses.whyCN: 制度把这一含义固定下来：无偏见的头脑变成一项可检查、可质疑的程序要求。

senses.title: Not harmed or impaired
senses.definition: old and rare, meaning not damaged or not made worse
senses.definitionCN: 古老而少用的义项，意为未受损害、未变糟
senses.example: The old pledge was to return the land unprejudiced by war.
senses.exampleCN: 那项古老的约定是让土地不受战争损害地归还。
senses.why: This archaic sense keeps the older legal force of damage and does not describe opinion at all; it is listed for completeness.
senses.whyCN: 这个古旧义保留了 prejudice 早期的「损害」法律含义，与看法无关；列出它只为求完整，现代读者不必使用。

intro.en: Unprejudiced is the prefix un- added to the past participle of prejudice: Latin praeiudicium, a judgement given beforehand, through Old French.
intro.cn: unprejudiced 是前缀 un- 加在 prejudice 的过去分词上；prejudice 源自拉丁语 praeiudicium（事先给出的判决），经古法语传入英语。

items.en: Praejudicium combines prae-, before, and judicium, judgement, and names a decision reached ahead of the facts.
items.cn: praejudicium 由 prae-（在前）与 judicium（判断）构成，指在事情发生之前就先给出的判定。

items.en: Praeiudicialis and the verb praeiudicare also carry the legal sense of harm or damage to a right.
items.cn: praeiudicialis 与动词 praeiudicare 另有一层法律含义：对某项权利造成损害。

items.en: Prejudice enters French as a legal term for a decision or harm that settles a matter in advance.
items.cn: prejudice 作为法律术语进入法语，指提前了结某事的裁断或损害。

items.en: Prejudice arrives in English as a legal word, gradually widening to mean a fixed opinion held before the facts are known.
items.cn: prejudice 以法律用语的身份进入英语，之后语义逐渐放宽，指在弄清事实之前就固定的看法。

items.en: Un- is prefixed to prejudiced to name a mind free from such a prior judgement; the form is chiefly modern and somewhat formal.
items.cn: un- 加到 prejudiced 之前，用来指不受这种预判影响的头脑；这一写法主要属现代英语，并以正式语域为主。

note.en: Unprejudiced sits inside the prejudice word family, and it is close to the ordinary words for being fair and neutral.
note.cn: unprejudiced 属于 prejudice 词族，意义靠近日常用来说「公正」「中立」的一群词。

entries.definition: having an unfair opinion formed without knowing the facts
entries.definitionCN: 事先形成不公正看法的，正好是 unprejudiced 的反面

entries.definition: an unfair feeling or opinion formed beforehand
entries.definitionCN: prejudice 指事先形成的不公正感受或看法，是 unprejudiced 所依赖的基础词

entries.definition: harmful to someone or something
entries.definitionCN: 有损害的；不利的，保留了 prejudice 早期的「损害」含义

entries.definition: a judgement made before all the facts are known
entries.definitionCN: 在了解全部事实之前就做出的判断，字面正是「预先判断」

entries.definition: not supporting one side more than another
entries.definitionCN: 不偏向任何一方，最常用于裁判与法官

entries.definition: showing no favour to one side or the other
entries.definitionCN: 没有倾向性的，语气比 unprejudiced 更直白、更常用

entries.definition: not taking sides in a disagreement
entries.definitionCN: 在争论中不站队，强调位置居中而未必强调判断开放

normalIntro.en: Unprejudiced is un- plus pre-judge: a judge who has not issued a verdict before hearing the evidence.
normalIntro.cn: unprejudiced 就是 un- 加上「预先判断」：一位还没听证据就先不宣判的法官。

normal.en: Split it as un + prejudiced, and note that prejudiced means having already made up your mind.
normal.cn: 把它拆成 un 加 prejudiced，而 prejudiced 指的是已经拿定主意、先有了看法。

normal.en: The Old French and Latin root pairs before with judgement, so the whole word is about judging too early.
normal.cn: 古法语与拉丁语词根把 before 和 judgment 放在一起，所以整个词都在说「判断得太早」。

normal.en: Unlike biased, unprejudiced is marked as formal and appears mostly before words like mind, view, and observer.
normal.cn: 与 biased 相比，unprejudiced 属正式语域，多出现在 mind、view、observer 这类词之前。

normal.en: Note the spelling: an e in the middle and an ed at the end, and no double d.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：中间有 e，词尾有 ed，而且没有双写的 d。

normal.en: Use the more common unprejudiced adjective for people, and say without prejudice when the phrasing is awkward.
normal.cn: 形容人时可用这个形容词，句子读起来别扭时也可以改用 without prejudice 这样的短语。

abstract.en: Picture a pair of tinted glasses being taken off, and the colours behind them turning true again.
abstract.cn: 想象取下一副有色眼镜，镜后的颜色重新变得真实。（对应第 1 个义项：判断中没有偏向）

abstract.en: Hold a door slightly open so an unexpected guest could still walk in.
abstract.cn: 把门留出一条缝，让意想不到的来客还能进来。（对应第 2 个义项：愿意接受相反的证据）

abstract.en: See a queue where every face is judged only by the ticket held in hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一条队伍里，每个人只凭手里的票据被评判。（对应第 3 个义项：不因种族、地域或阶层区别待人）

examples.en: The tribunal promised an unprejudiced review of every complaint.
examples.cn: 法庭承诺对每一项投诉进行无偏见的审查。

examples.en: Readers came away with a more unprejudiced understanding of the reform.
examples.cn: 读者读完对这场改革有了更不带成见的理解。

examples.en: Try to keep an unprejudiced mind when the first results look bad.
examples.cn: 当最初的结果不好看时，尽量保持一颗无偏见的头脑。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不偏执的」——先不急着站边，别人说什么都听一听，就是不偏执、不带偏见。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 prae-（在前）+ judicium（判断）→ praeiudicium（预先作出的判决）→ 古法语 prejudice → 英语 prejudice（偏见；成见）→ prejudiced（有偏见的）→ un- + prejudiced → unprejudiced，核心义「不在看清事实前抢先判定」。

sensesIntro.en: Unprejudiced starts with judgement free from bias, widens to an open attitude, moves into fairness between social groups, then to views not warped by self-interest, to a state required of officials, and finally to an almost obsolete sense of being unharmed.
sensesIntro.cn: unprejudiced 起于判断不带偏向，扩展为开放的态度，再到种族与阶层意义上的公平，接着指见解未受私利扭曲，又成为制度对官员的要求，最后还残留一个几乎废弃的「未受损害」义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: tinted glasses taken off, and the colours of the world returning to their own tones.
core.cn: 核心意象：摘下有色眼镜，世界的颜色回到它本来的样子。

branches.en: The personal branch: no prejudice in the mind of the judge or observer.
branches.cn: 个人分支：裁判或观察者心里没有偏见。

branches.en: The attitude branch: the mind stays open to what might contradict it.
branches.cn: 态度分支：头脑对可能与之相反的东西保持开放。

branches.en: The social branch: no group is judged in advance.
branches.cn: 社会分支：没有任何群体被预先评判。

branches.en: One branch is about the judgement, the other about the official who must produce it.
branches.cn: 两条分支：一条落在判断本身，一条落在必须拿出这种判断的官员身上。

branches.en: The archaic branch borrows prejudice in its old legal sense of harm.
branches.cn: 古旧分支借用了 prejudice 早期表示「损害」的法律含义。

intro.en: Unprejudiced is the negative prefix un- on prejudiced, and the prejudic- family runs through prejudice, prejudiced, prejudicial, and the spelling variant pre-judge.
intro.cn: unprejudiced 用否定前缀 un- 加在 prejudiced 上，prejudic- 词族贯穿 prejudice、prejudiced、prejudicial，以及拼写变体 pre-judge。

latinIntro.en: Latin gives the core of the family: prae- meaning before and judicium meaning judgement, joined in praeiudicium and in the verb praeiudicare.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了这个词族的核心：prae- 意为「在前」，judicium 意为「判断」，二者合成 praeiudicium 与动词 praeiudicare。

items.example: The prefix un- reverses the sense of prejudiced.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 prejudiced 的意思反过来。

items.example: Judge is the everyday word behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: judge 是整个词族赖以为基础的日常词，意为判断。

items.meaning: the act of forming an opinion
items.example: Judgement matches Latin judicium.
items.exampleCN: judgement 对应拉丁语的 judicium。

items.example: The prefix pre- says the judging comes too early.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 pre- 表示判断来得太早。

items.example: Prejudice is the noun that the whole family grows from.
items.exampleCN: prejudice 是这个词族生长的名词基础。

items.example: The suffix -ed turns prejudice into an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 把 prejudice 变成形容词。

items.example: Unprejudiced is mostly written before mind or view.
items.exampleCN: unprejudiced 多数时候写在 mind 或 view 前面。

items.example: The suffix -ed builds prejudiced, and un- then negates it.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 prejudiced，随后 un- 再将其否定。

items.example: The suffix -ial forms prejudicial from the Latin stem.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ial 从拉丁词干构成 prejudicial。

items.example: The suffix -ness keeps the same pattern as in unprejudicedness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 与 unprejudicedness 的构词方式相同。

latinEntries.meaning: to judge in advance; to prejudice

definition_zh: 结束引文；引文结束；取消对……的引用（技术支持或系统用语）
definition_en: to mark the end of a quotation, often spoken after someone else has been quoted, or to remove quotation marks
core_image: 右手在空中画一个收拢的引号，把别人说过的话重新关上
scene: 记者转述财政部长的话时，念完便朝摄影机晃了晃手，示意那段原话到此结束。The minister called the plan, and I am giving your readers his exact words here, a modest start, unquote.
sceneCN: 这里 unquote 是「引文结束」（第 2 个义项：口语中提示引文的结束，常与 quote 成对使用）；句意：部长把这项计划称作（这里是照原话念的）一个不大的开始，引文结束。

collocations.zh: （先说）引文开始，（再说）引文结束
结束这段引述，与 end quote 同义
取消对这段文字的引用
取消对地址的引用或处理转义

derivatives.zh: 未加引号的；未被引用的；未被报价的，也可以充当 unquote 的过去分词
引用；引述，unquote 正是它加否定前缀 un- 的反向动作
取消引用的处理，由 unquote 加 -ing 构成，多见于技术文档

senses.title: To close a quotation
senses.definition: to bring a quotation to an end, spoken after the quoted words so the listener knows the quotation has stopped
senses.definitionCN: 为一段引文收尾；在念完被引内容之后说出，让听者知道引述已经停止
senses.example: He said, I have nothing to add, unquote, and left the room.
senses.exampleCN: 他说「我没有要补充的了」，引文结束，然后离开了房间。
senses.why: Quote originally marked the start of reproduced words, so un- gives the matching move that closes them again.
senses.whyCN: quote 原本用来标记照搬他人话语的开始，加上 un- 就得到了与之配对、把这段话重新关上的动作。

senses.title: The spoken signal that a quotation has ended
senses.definition: used as an interjection when speaking, to signal the end of words that someone else said
senses.definitionCN: 口语中作感叹词使用，提示刚刚那几句话是被引述的、并非说话者本人的原意
senses.example: She is, quote, extremely busy, unquote, and cannot see anyone today.
senses.exampleCN: 她「非常忙」，引文到此为止，今天谁也见不了。
senses.why: Speech has no quotation marks, so the word becomes a sound effect for punctuation and often carries irony toward the quoted words.
senses.whyCN: 口头说话没有引号可用，这个词便成了标点的音效；它常带着一丝反讽，暗示被引的话未必可信。

senses.title: To remove quotation marks, in computing
senses.titleCN: 取消引用；去掉引号（计算机用语）
senses.definition: in computing, to remove quotation marks from data or from a command line before the text is used
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机语境中，在使用文本之前把引号从数据或命令行里去掉
senses.example: The parser will unquote the value before it stores it.
senses.exampleCN: 解析器会在存储之前把这个值上的引号去掉。
senses.why: The computing sense generalises the move from closing a quotation to stripping its marks, and it keeps the same un- shape.
senses.whyCN: 计算机义把「结束引文」推广为「剥去引号标记」的动作，构词方式仍是 un-，只是对象从说话变成了数据。

senses.title: To return a quoted item to its original form
senses.definition: to turn a quoted or encoded expression back into the plain form it stood for
senses.definitionCN: 把被引用或被转义编码的表达式还原为它所代表的普通形式
senses.example: Some tools unquote a URL before passing it on.
senses.exampleCN: 有些工具会先把网址里的转义还原，再继续向下传递。
senses.why: Dictionary entries record this technical sense of converting a quoted expression back, which extends the idea of undoing the quoting step.
senses.whyCN: 词典记载了这层技术含义：把被引用的表达式还原回去；这等于把「加引号」这一步原样撤销。

intro.en: Unquote is modern English un- added to quote, whose source is a rounding word for how many, from Latin quot through Medieval Latin quotare and Old French.
intro.cn: unquote 是近代英语中 un- 加在 quote 上的构词；quote 的源头是拉丁语 quot（多少），经中世纪拉丁语 quotare 与古法语传入英语。

items.en: Quot means how many, and quotus means of what number; the family is about counting rather than speaking.
items.cn: quot 意为「多少」，quotus 意为「属于第几号的」；这个词族原本与计数有关，而非与说话有关。

items.en: Quotare comes to mean to number chapters or to mark a passage by its number.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 quotare 意为「给章节编号」或「用编号标出某段文字」。

items.en: Coter carries the marking sense into Old French as a way of numbering and labelling texts.
items.cn: coter 把「标记编号」的含义带入古法语，用于给文本编号和标注。

items.en: First recorded in 1387, the English verb means to mark a book with chapter numbers or marginal references.
items.cn: 该动词在英语中首见于一三八七年，意为在书上标注章节编号或页边注记。

items.en: The sense moves to citing a passage as authority, then to repeating exact words by late seventeenth century, and to stating a price in the nineteenth.
items.cn: 此后词义先转向「引证某段文字作为依据」，到十七世纪后期才指「照原话复述」，十九世纪又添上「报价」的用法。

items.en: Un- is added to quote to close a spoken quotation; the form is first recorded in dictionary evidence of the mid twentieth century and spreads fastest in broadcast speech.
items.cn: un- 加在 quote 上用来结束口头引文；词典证据显示这一写法在二十世纪中叶已经出现，并在广播口语中迅速普及。

note.en: Unquote belongs to the quotation family built on quote, and in speech it pairs with the words people use for quoting and citing.
note.cn: unquote 属于以 quote 为基础的引用词族，在日常口语里又常与表示引用、引述的一群词配成对。

entries.definition: to repeat someone else words exactly
entries.definitionCN: quote 指照原话复述他人的话；unquote 是与之配对的收尾动作

entries.definition: not placed inside quotation marks
entries.definitionCN: 未加引号的；也可以是 unquote 的过去分词与过去式形式

entries.definition: the words someone has quoted
entries.definitionCN: 引语；引用，指被引述的那段话本身

entries.definition: to repeat someone words in a way that changes their intended point
entries.definitionCN: 断章取义地引用；这个词组与 unquote 都围绕引用展开，但重点是引用方式走样

entries.definition: the words spoken to show that a quotation has ended
entries.definitionCN: 说话或口述校对时用来表示引文结束的固定说法

entries.definition: to quote a passage as evidence or support
entries.definitionCN: 引用某段文字作为依据或证据，比 quote 更正式

entries.definition: to repeat someone words inaccurately
entries.definitionCN: 错误地引用别人的话，是引用词族里常见的问题词

normalIntro.en: Unquote is un- plus quote: the voice puts a full stop on the borrowed words and hands the sentence back to the speaker.
normalIntro.cn: unquote 就是 un- 加 quote：把借来的话打个句号，再把句子交还给说话的人。

normal.en: The pair quote and unquote works like opening and closing a speech version of quotation marks.
normal.cn: quote 与 unquote 这对词，就像在口语里代替引号的「开」与「合」。

normal.en: Note the spelling: quote has no second c, unlike quotation, which keeps the t sound in a different shape.
normal.cn: 注意拼写：quote 里没有第二个 c；名词 quotation 的拼写形状与之不同，读音也跟着变化。

normal.en: Quote unquote, said together before a word, marks it as someone else label with a hint of doubt.
normal.cn: quote unquote 连说、放在某个词之前，表示那是别人的说法，并带一点怀疑的味道。

normal.en: In computing, un- still means undo, so unquote undoes the quoting done by the previous step.
normal.cn: 在计算机语境里 un- 仍表示「撤销」，所以 unquote 就是撤销上一步所做的引用处理。

normal.en: Because the source of quote is a counting word, it gained its speaking sense late; the modern un- form is much younger still.
normal.cn: 因为 quote 源头是个计数词，它获得「引述」义很晚，而现代这个带 un- 的形式出现得更晚。

abstract.en: Picture a finger lifting to close a pair of invisible quotation marks in the air.
abstract.cn: 想象抬起手指，把空中一对看不见的引号合上。（对应第 1 个义项：为引文收尾）

abstract.en: Hear a broadcaster say the quoted words in a different voice, then drop back to their own.
abstract.cn: 想象播音员用另一种声音念引文，念完又换回自己的声音。（对应第 2 个义项：口语中提示引文结束）

abstract.en: Watch a machine snip two small marks off a string before packing it into a box.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器把一串字符上的两个小记号剪掉，再装进盒子里。（对应第 3 个义项：在计算中去除引号）

examples.en: The editor asked the reporter to unquote the phrase so it matched the written source.
examples.cn: 编辑要求记者把那个短语的引号去掉，使其与书面来源一致。

examples.en: He described the meeting as unquote, a lively exchange of views, unquote.
examples.cn: 他把这次会面形容为「一场热烈的意见交换」，引文到此结束。

examples.en: The script will unquote every value before it writes the table.
examples.cn: 脚本会在写入表格之前去掉每一个值上的引号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安拷特」——话音刚落，把引号一收，这段「拷来」的话就归档了。这只是读音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 quot（多少）+ quotus（第几号的）→ 中世纪拉丁语 quotare（给章节编号）→ 古法语 coter → 英语 quote（引用；引述）→ un- + quote → unquote，核心义「结束一段引用」。

sensesIntro.en: Unquote grew out of the speaking habit of announcements: it opens as the device that closes a quotation, then becomes the spoken signal itself, and in modern computing extends to stripping quotation marks and restoring quoted data.
sensesIntro.cn: unquote 脱胎于口头转述的习惯：先是为引文收尾的动作，再成为口语里提示引文结束的信号，进入计算机语境后又扩展为去掉引号、还原被引用数据等用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand drawing a closing quotation mark in the air after the borrowed words.
core.cn: 核心意象：念完借来的话，手在空中画出收拢的引号。

branches.en: The action branch: to bring a quotation to its end.
branches.cn: 动作分支：为一段引文划上终点。

branches.en: The spoken branch: the interjection that stands in for quotation marks.
branches.cn: 口语分支：用感叹词代替书面引号。

branches.en: The technical branch: stripping marks and restoring quoted data.
branches.cn: 技术分支：剥去引号，并还原被引用的数据。

branches.en: Both live in speech, one as what a speaker does, the other as what listeners hear.
branches.cn: 两者都在口语里运行：一个描述说话者做的动作，一个描述听者听到的信号。

branches.en: Closing a quotation and removing quotation marks are the same gesture, one by voice and one by code.
branches.cn: 结束引文与去掉引号是同一个手势，一个用声音完成，一个用代码完成。

intro.en: Unquote is the negative prefix un- on quote; the family on quote runs through quotation, quotation mark, misquote, and unquoted.
intro.cn: unquote 是否定前缀 un- 加在 quote 上，quote 词族还包括 quotation、quotation mark、misquote 与 unquoted。

latinIntro.en: The prefix un- is Germanic, not Latin; the Latin part is quot, how many, which gave the numbering sense and much later the quoting sense.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 un- 属日耳曼语，不来自拉丁语；来自拉丁语的部分是 quot（多少），它先带来「编号」义，很久以后才带来「引用」义。

items.example: The prefix un- makes unquote the reverse of quote.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使 unquote 成为 quote 的反向动作。

items.example: Quote opens a quotation and unquote closes it.
items.exampleCN: quote 开启一段引文，unquote 把它关闭。

items.example: Unquote is usually spoken between commas.
items.exampleCN: unquote 在口语中两边常各有一个停顿。

items.example: The suffix -ation forms quotation from quote.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ation 把 quote 变成 quotation。

items.example: Quotation is the noun that most often appears in written work.
items.exampleCN: quotation 是书面写作中最常出现的名词形式。

items.example: The prefix mis- forms misquote with the idea of quoting wrongly.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 mis- 与 quote 组合成误引的 misquote。

items.example: Misquote is the opposite error to unquote.
items.exampleCN: misquote 与 unquote 各自对应引用过程中的不同问题。

items.meaningCN: 过去分词与形容词后缀
items.example: The suffix -ed gives unquoted.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ed 构成 unquoted。

items.example: Unquoted content is often treated as plain text.
items.exampleCN: 未加引号的内容通常被当作普通文本处理。

items.meaning: a printed or written pair of marks around quoted words
items.example: Quotation mark names the sign that unquote stands in for.
items.exampleCN: quotation mark 指的那个符号，正是 unquote 在口语里代替的东西。

latinEntries.meaning: of what number; which in order
to number; to mark by number

definition_zh: 不切实际的；不现实的；脱离实际的；不真实的
definition_en: not based on what can really happen or on how people and things really are
core_image: 一张地图上画着直通山顶的平路，而山其实陡得站不住脚
scene: 室友说两年内攒够首付，你看着他的工资单直摇头。It may be unrealistic to expect a miracle in one week.
sceneCN: 这里 unrealistic 是「不切实际的」（第 1 个义项：目标、计划不符合真实条件）；句意：指望着在一个星期里出现奇迹，恐怕是不切实际的。

derivatives.zh: unrealistic 加 -ally 构成副词，义为「不切实际地」
-ism 名词后缀，指文学艺术中缺乏真实感的手法，义为「不真实主义」
un- 与 reality 结合，指缺乏真实感的状态，义为「不真实」
un- 加 real 构成，义为「不真实的；虚幻的」

senses.title: Not possible in real terms
senses.definition: too hopeful or ambitious to actually happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 过于乐观或宏大，以至于真的发生或成功不了
senses.example: Expecting the bridge to be finished this year is unrealistic.
senses.exampleCN: 指望这座桥今年完工是不切实际的。
senses.why: The prefix un- reverses the -istic quality of real: the plan has lost touch with what the world really allows.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 否定了 real 的真实性质：这个计划已经和现实允许的条件脱了节。

senses.title: Not how things really are
senses.definition: showing people or events in a way that is too simple or perfect to match real life
senses.definitionCN: 以过于简单或完美的样子呈现人或事，与真实生活不符
senses.example: The detective film gives a very unrealistic picture of police work.
senses.exampleCN: 这部侦探片对警察工作的描绘非常不真实。
senses.why: Once un- takes away real, the result can also describe content rather than a goal: a story that does not look like life.
senses.whyCN: un- 取消了 real 之后，这个词也能用来描述内容而不是目标：一个看着不像真实生活的故事。

senses.title: Too hopeful in love or ideals
senses.definition: based on an ideal so high or perfect that ordinary people cannot reach it
senses.definitionCN: 基于高到或完美到普通人达不到的理想
senses.example: He held an unrealistic idea of romance from old films.
senses.exampleCN: 他从老电影里得来一种不现实的浪漫观念。
senses.why: The ideal picture in the mind has been drawn without any contact with real people.
senses.whyCN: 脑海中的理想图景完全没有和真实的人打过交道就被画出来了。

senses.title: Impossible to keep up in work or study
senses.definition: too demanding for the time or effort that is actually available
senses.definitionCN: 对实际可用的时间或精力来说要求过高
senses.example: The workload for the first week was clearly unrealistic.
senses.exampleCN: 第一周的工作量显然不合理。
senses.why: The same logic applies to schedules: they are not real, because real days only have so many hours.
senses.whyCN: 同样的逻辑也适用于日程：它们不真实，因为真实的一天只有那么多小时。

senses.title: Missed by others as out of touch
senses.definition: used to describe a person or proposal that others judge to be out of touch with facts
senses.definitionCN: 用来形容被他人判定为脱离事实的人或提议
senses.example: Critics called the plan unrealistic and underfunded.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者称这个计划不切实际且资金不足。
senses.why: In review and debate, un- becomes a judgement: the speaker says the idea has no ground in real conditions.
senses.whyCN: 在评论和辩论中，un- 变成一种评判：说话人认为这个想法在真实条件下没有立足点。

intro.en: Unrealistic is a learned English formation: the prefix un- plus realistic, which itself comes from real and the ending -istic.
intro.cn: unrealistic 是英语里的学术式构词：前缀 un- 加 realistic，而 realistic 又由 real 加词尾 -istic 组成。

items.en: Late Latin realis means belonging to things, from Latin res, a thing.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 realis 意为「属于事物的」，源于拉丁语 res（事物）。

items.en: Middle English real enters from Old French reel with the sense of actually existing.
items.cn: 中古英语 real 经古法语 reel 进入英语，表示「实际存在的」。

items.en: The adjective realistic develops from realism and rises with the realistic novel.
items.cn: 形容词 realistic 由 realism 派生，随现实主义小说一起流行。

items.en: Unrealistic is formed by adding un- to realistic, following the un- able pattern of unreal and unrealizable.
items.cn: unrealistic 由 un- 加 realistic 构成，延续 unreal、unrealizable 这类加 un- 的模式。

items.en: The word spreads in planning, education, and criticism of policy.
items.cn: 这个词在规划、教育和政策批评中广泛使用。

note.en: Unrealistic is close to its family words unreal, unreality, and unrealistically, and to ordinary words for ideas that miss real life.
note.cn: unrealistic 与同族的 unreal、unreality、unrealistically 相邻，也与围绕「脱离现实」的普通词相邻。

entries.definition: seeming not to belong to actual life
entries.definitionCN: 似乎不属于现实生活的；虚幻的

entries.definition: the quality of lacking a sense of real life
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏真实感的状态

entries.definition: in a way that ignores real conditions
entries.definitionCN: 不切实际地

entries.definition: the treatment of things as they really are
entries.definitionCN: 写实的风格；现实主义

entries.definition: not sensible or workable in real use
entries.definitionCN: 不实用的；行不通的

entries.definition: believing in high perfect standards rather than real ones
entries.definitionCN: 理想化的；理想主义的

entries.definition: based on hope rather than on facts
entries.definitionCN: 一厢情愿的

normalIntro.en: Unrealistic is un- plus realistic: strip away the real, and what remains cannot happen.
normalIntro.cn: unrealistic 就是 un- 加 realistic：把「真实」剥掉，剩下的东西就不可能发生。

normal.en: un- is a negative meaning prefix, so unrealistic is the opposite of realistic.
normal.cn: un- 是表示否定的前缀，所以 unrealistic 就是 realistic 的反面。

normal.en: Unrealistic expectations are the most common phrase, often in advice and reviews.
normal.cn: unrealistic expectations 是最常见的搭配，常用于建议和评论。

normal.en: The adverb unrealistically keeps the same meaning in front of verbs and adjectives.
normal.cn: 副词 unrealistically 放在动词或形容词前面，意思不变。

normal.en: Compare unreality: unrealistic judges a plan, unreality names a feeling or a style.
normal.cn: 对比 unreality：unrealistic 评判一个计划，unreality 命名一种感觉或风格。

normal.en: In IELTS writing, call a target clearly beyond reach, not just difficult: unrealistic, not hard.
normal.cn: 在雅思写作里，说一个目标明显够不着而不只是很难，要用 unrealistic 而不是 hard。

abstract.en: Picture a ladder propped against the sky with no ground under its feet.
abstract.cn: 想象一架梯子搭在云上，脚下却没有地面。

abstract.en: Imagine a film in which every street is spotless and every crowd smiles.
abstract.cn: 想象一部电影，每条街都一尘不染，每个人都笑盈盈。

abstract.en: Think of a heart drawn around a candle held on top of a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗画在蜡烛周围的心，被摆在墙头。

examples.en: Setting a daily target of ten thousand words is unrealistic for a beginner.
examples.cn: 对初学者来说，每天一万词的目标是不切实际的。

examples.en: The plan looked good on paper but was unrealistic in cost.
examples.cn: 这个计划纸面上很好，但成本上并不现实。

examples.en: Advertisers often create unrealistic images of family life.
examples.cn: 广告商常常塑造出不真实的家庭生活形象。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安瑞丽丝提克」——安下心来才谈得上瑞丽，硬把梦想说成能提克现实，就是不切实际；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: un-（否定）+ real（真实的，源自拉丁语 res 即「事物」）+ -istic（……性质的），字面义「不具备真实性质的」，核心义「与真实不符」。

sensesIntro.en: Unrealistic describes goals that cannot be reached, content that does not match life, and ideals or schedules that ask for too much.
sensesIntro.cn: unrealistic 先指够不着的目标，再指与现实不符的内容，也指要求过高的理想或日程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a map that draws a flat road up a mountain.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上把通往山顶的路画成一条平路。

branches.en: Goals beyond real conditions form the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 超出真实条件的目标构成日常义项。

branches.en: Content that does not look like life is the descriptive sense.
branches.cn: 看起来不像真实生活的内容是描述性义项。

branches.en: Ideals held by a person, and judgements passed by critics, share the same gap from reality.
branches.cn: 人怀有的理想和批评者做出的评判，都源于与现实的同一处差距。

branches.en: Schedules fail for the same reason: real time is limited.
branches.cn: 日程之所以不合理，原因相同：真实的时间是有限的。

branches.en: Expectations and stories can both become unrealistic when they escape the real.
branches.cn: 期望和故事一旦脱离真实，都会变得不切实。

intro.en: Unrealistic carries the negative prefix un-, the root real, and the adjective ending -istic, with a whole word family behind it.
intro.cn: unrealistic 由否定前缀 un-、词根 real 和形容词词尾 -istic 组成，背后是一整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin res means a thing, and realis means belonging to things; English real comes through Old French reel.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 res 意为「事物」，realis 意为「属于事物的」；英语 real 经古法语 reel 传来。

items.example: The prefix un- reverses the adjective realistic.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 反转了形容词 realistic 的意思。

items.example: Real is the root adjective of the family.
items.exampleCN: real 是这一词族的词根形容词。

items.example: The suffix -istic turns realism into realistic.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -istic 把 realism 变成 realistic。

items.meaning: a style that shows life as it is
items.example: Realism is the noun built on real.
items.exampleCN: realism 是由 real 派生的名词。

items.meaning: based on what can really happen
items.example: Realistic is the positive partner of the target word.
items.exampleCN: realistic 是目标词的肯定对应词。

items.example: The ending -ally forms unrealistically.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ally 构成 unrealistically。

items.example: Unreal shows the shortest un- form.
items.exampleCN: unreal 展示了最短的加 un- 形式。

items.example: Unreality is the noun of the un- family.
items.exampleCN: unreality 是加 un- 词族的名词。

items.example: Unrealizable applies the same un- logic to realize.
items.exampleCN: unrealizable 把同样的 un- 逻辑用在 realize 上。

definition_zh: 未登记的；未注册的；未挂号寄出的
definition_en: not officially recorded on a list, register, or official record
core_image: 一本摊开的名册，某一页上整整齐齐都是名字，只有一行空在那里
scene: 小狗出生后被抱回家，主人忙着取名，却忘了给它办牌照。The council warned that unregistered landlords could face heavy fines.
sceneCN: 这里 unregistered 是「未登记的」（第 1 个义项：未列入官方名册）；句意：市政部门警告说，未登记的房东可能面临高额罚款。

derivatives.zh: un- 与 register 结合，义为「注销；取消登记」
register 加 -ation，义为「登记；注册；挂号」
-ar 后缀，指负责登记事务的人，义为「登记员」
-ry 后缀，指登记记录的册子或场所，义为「登记册；登记处」

senses.title: Not entered in an official list
senses.definition: not recorded in a list kept by an authority, such as a roll of residents, births, or land
senses.definitionCN: 没有被官方机构列入名册，例如住户册、出生登记簿或土地登记簿
senses.example: The twins were born at home and remained unregistered for years.
senses.exampleCN: 这对双胞胎在家出生，好几年都没有登记。
senses.why: The prefix un- reverses register, whose Latin base means to carry back into a written list.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 反转了 register，而后者的拉丁语词基意为「把东西带回并写进名册」。

senses.title: Not formally registered for a purpose
senses.definition: not formally enrolled with an authority for a legal or commercial purpose, as with a company or a trademark
senses.definitionCN: 没有为法律或商业目的正式向主管部门登记，例如公司或商标
senses.example: An unregistered trademark still needs proof of use in court.
senses.exampleCN: 未注册的商标在法庭上仍然需要证明使用情况。
senses.why: A list that carries legal force turns registration into a status, so unregistered becomes a legal label.
senses.whyCN: 当名册具有法律效力时，登记就成了一种身份，未注册也就成了法律上的标签。

senses.title: Not recorded by a machine
senses.definition: not detected or recorded by an instrument or system that normally keeps a record
senses.definitionCN: 没有被通常负责记录的仪器或系统侦测或记录下来
senses.example: The app left the unregistered device off the network.
senses.exampleCN: 这个应用把那台未登记的设备挡在了网络之外。
senses.why: The modern system keeps its own list, so a gadget outside the list is literally not written in.
senses.whyCN: 现代系统各自有一份名单，不在名单上的设备字面上就是「没有被写进去」。

senses.title: Sent without special tracking
senses.definition: sent by post without the extra fee that gives the sender a record of delivery
senses.definitionCN: 寄信时不付额外费用，寄件人拿不到投递记录
senses.example: Send the documents by unregistered mail if speed does not matter.
senses.exampleCN: 如果不赶时间，就用未挂号信件寄文件。
senses.why: Postal registers once recorded letters one by one; mail left off that book travels unwatched.
senses.whyCN: 邮政登记簿曾逐封记下信件，没进这本簿子的邮件就无人看管地旅行。

intro.en: Unregistered is un- plus registered, built on register, which came through Old French from Latin registrum.
intro.cn: unregistered 是 un- 加 registered，而 registered 由 register 构成；register 经古法语源自拉丁语 registrum。

items.en: Medieval Latin registrum means a list or a register, probably from Latin regesta, a record.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 registrum 意为名册或登记簿，一般认为来自拉丁语 regesta（记录）。

items.en: Old French registre names the book in which matters are entered.
items.cn: 古法语 registre 指把事项记进去的册子。

items.en: Middle English register enters as a noun for an official record.
items.cn: 中古英语 register 以名词身份进入，指官方记录。

items.en: The verb to register develops, meaning to enter a name in a book.
items.cn: 动词 register 出现，意为把名字写进册子里。

items.en: Registered appears as the participle adjective, and unregistered follows by negation.
items.cn: 分词形容词 registered 出现，随后通过加否定前缀产生 unregistered。

items.en: The word spreads to vehicles, land, trademarks, and digital devices.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到车辆、土地、商标和数字设备领域。

note.en: Unregistered is the negation of registered and stands beside register, registration, and enrol in the world of official lists.
note.cn: unregistered 是 registered 的否定形式，与 register、registration 以及围绕官方名册的 enrol 相邻。

entries.definition: to enter a name or detail in an official list
entries.definitionCN: 把名字或细节登记进官方名册

entries.definition: the act of making an official record
entries.definitionCN: 登记；注册行为

entries.definition: an official who keeps records
entries.definitionCN: 负责登记记录的官员

entries.definition: officially recorded on a list
entries.definitionCN: 已登记的；已注册的

entries.definition: not supported by official papers
entries.definitionCN: 没有官方文件记录的

entries.definition: not having the official permission the law requires
entries.definitionCN: 未获执照的；没有许可的

entries.definition: not recognized by an authority
entries.definitionCN: 非官方的；未经认可的

normalIntro.en: Unregistered is simply un- in front of registered: the name is missing from the book.
normalIntro.cn: unregistered 就是 registered 前面加 un-：名字没有出现在册子上。

normal.en: Registered is the past participle of register, so unregistered describes a state.
normal.cn: registered 是 register 的过去分词，所以 unregistered 描述的是一种状态。

normal.en: The noun registration and the person noun registrar share the same base.
normal.cn: 名词 registration 和指人的 registrar 共享同一个词基。

normal.en: Compare unlicensed: unregistered focuses on the missing record, unlicensed on the missing permit.
normal.cn: 对比 unlicensed：unregistered 侧重缺记录，unlicensed 侧重缺执照。

normal.en: The phrase unregistered trademark often appears with the tiny letters beside a brand name.
normal.cn: unregistered trademark 这个说法常和品牌名旁边的小字母一起出现。

normal.en: In legal writing, unregistered land is land whose title is not yet recorded.
normal.cn: 在法律文本里，unregistered land 指产权尚未记录的土地。

abstract.en: Picture a long roll of names with one blank line in the middle.
abstract.cn: 想象一长卷名字，中间空着一行。

abstract.en: Imagine a sticker on a shirt collar with no name printed on it.
abstract.cn: 想象衣领上的标签上什么都没有印。

abstract.en: Think of a device glowing at the door of a network that will not open.
abstract.cn: 想象一台设备在网络门口发着光，门却不开。

examples.en: Many informal workers remain unregistered and have no pension.
examples.cn: 许多非正式工人一直没有登记，也没有养老金。

examples.en: An unregistered vehicle may be taken off the road by the police.
examples.cn: 未登记的车辆可能会被警察扣下、不许上路。

examples.en: The tiny letters beside the logo show it is an unregistered mark.
examples.cn: 标识旁边的小字母表明这是一个未注册商标。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安雷吉斯特德」——按雷打不动去登记，才会出现在名册上；少了这一步，就成了「未登记」；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: un-（否定）+ register（登记；名册，源自拉丁语 registrum「记录簿」）+ -ed（分词词尾），字面义「没有被登记过的」，核心义「不在官方名册上」。

sensesIntro.en: Unregistered starts from a missing entry in an official book and moves to legal status, technical systems, and ordinary post.
sensesIntro.cn: unregistered 从官方名册上缺的一笔出发，延伸到法律身份、技术系统和普通邮政。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a register page where one line stays blank.
core.cn: 核心意象：登记册的某一页上，空着一行。

branches.en: Missing from a record kept by an authority is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 在主管机构的名册上缺位，是基本义项。

branches.en: Legal registration makes the word a status label.
branches.cn: 法律登记让这个词成为身份标签。

branches.en: A digital system keeps its own list, so a device outside it is unregistered.
branches.cn: 数字系统有自己的名单，名单外的设备就是未登记的。

branches.en: Postal records gave the same word a use for mail.
branches.cn: 邮政记录让同一个词也用到了信件上。

branches.en: Both a person off the roll and a letter off the postal book share the missing entry.
branches.cn: 名册外的人与邮政簿外的信件，都共享「缺失的那一笔」。

intro.en: Unregistered gathers the negative prefix un-, the verb register from Latin registrum, and the participial ending -ed.
intro.cn: unregistered 汇集了否定前缀 un-、源自拉丁语 registrum 的动词 register 和分词词尾 -ed。

latinIntro.en: Latin registrum or regesta names a record book, and Latin re- plus gerere gives the idea of carrying matters back.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 registrum 或 regesta 指名册，拉丁语 re- 加 gerere 表达「把事带回来」的意思。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the participle registered.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定了分词 registered。

items.example: The ending -ed marks a finished state.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 标记一种已完成的状态。

items.example: Register is the base of the whole group.
items.exampleCN: register 是整组词的词基。

items.example: The ending -ation forms registration.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ation 构成 registration。

items.example: The ending -ar forms registrar.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ar 构成 registrar。

items.example: The ending -ry forms registry.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ry 构成 registry。

items.example: Registered is the direct opposite of the target word.
items.exampleCN: registered 是目标词的直接反义形式。

items.example: Unregister applies un- to the verb itself.
items.exampleCN: unregister 把 un- 直接加在动词上。

items.example: Registrant names the person who registers.
items.exampleCN: registrant 指办理登记的人。

definition_zh: （爱）得不到回应的；单相思的；无回报的
definition_en: felt strongly for someone but not given back in return
core_image: 一个人把花递过篱笆，另一只手始终没有伸过来接
scene: 他每天替她在图书馆留位置，她却从来没有坐过一次。He wrote poems about unrequited love for many years.
sceneCN: 这里 unrequited 是「得不到回应的」（第 1 个义项：付出的爱没有回流）；句意：多年来他写的都是关于单相思的诗。

collocations.zh: 单相思；得不到回应的爱

derivatives.zh: re- 加 quite，义为「回报；酬答」，其否定形式即 unrequited
-al 名词后缀，义为「回报；报答」
-ly 副词后缀，义为「以得不到回应的方式」

senses.title: Love that is not returned
senses.definition: describing romantic love that the other person does not feel back
senses.definitionCN: 形容对方并不以同样的感情相回的爱
senses.example: She never told him about her unrequited love.
senses.exampleCN: 她从未告诉他自己那份得不到回应的爱。
senses.why: The prefix un- denies requite, to give something back for something received, so love given has no return.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 否定了 requite（收到东西后回赠），所以付出的爱没有回流。

senses.title: Kindness that is never repaid
senses.titleCN: 不图回报的；未获回报的
senses.definition: describing care or kindness given without any return from the one who receives it
senses.definitionCN: 形容给予的关怀或好意没有得到接受者任何回报
senses.example: His unrequited kindness to the old man went on for years.
senses.exampleCN: 他对那位老人的好持续了好些年，却从未得到回报。
senses.why: The same denial applies to any favour: a gift handed over with nothing coming back.
senses.whyCN: 同样的否定也适用于任何恩惠：递出去的东西，什么也没有回返。

senses.title: Effort or service without recognition
senses.titleCN: 得不到回应的；无人认可的
senses.definition: describing effort or service that receives no thanks or reward from those it serves
senses.definitionCN: 形容所付出的努力或服务，没有得到服务对象的感谢或奖赏
senses.example: Years of unrequited effort left the team exhausted.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的白干让团队筋疲力尽。
senses.why: Work, like love and kindness, is something given, and un- says the return never arrives.
senses.whyCN: 努力和爱、好意一样都是「给予」的东西，un- 表示回报始终没有到来。

senses.title: Literary and poetic use
senses.definition: used in poetry and song to name a longing that the world or another person never answers
senses.definitionCN: 在诗歌和歌曲中，指世界或他人始终不回应的渴望
senses.example: The ballad turns unrequited longing into a kind of beauty.
senses.exampleCN: 这首民谣把无回报的思念化成了某种美。
senses.why: Literature keeps the oldest use alive and gives the missing response an emotional shape.
senses.whyCN: 文学作品让最古老的用法延续下来，并给缺失的回应赋予了情感的形状。

intro.en: Unrequited is un- plus the past participle requited, from the verb requite, which reached English through the re- and quite of Old French and Latin.
intro.cn: unrequited 是 un- 加过去分词 requited，后者来自动词 requite；requite 经古法语的 re- 与 quite 以及拉丁语词源进入英语。

items.en: Latin quietus means at rest or free from obligation, and re- means back.
items.cn: 拉丁语 quietus 意为安宁的、免除义务的，re- 意为「回」。

items.en: Old French quiter means to release from a debt or obligation.
items.cn: 古法语 quiter 意为免除债务或义务。

items.en: The verb requite appears, meaning to repay or give in return for something received.
items.cn: 动词 requite 出现，意为报答或对收到的给予回报。

items.en: Requited develops as a participle, and unrequited names a payment that never comes back.
items.cn: 分词 requited 形成，unrequited 则指始终不回来的偿付。

items.en: Unrequited love becomes a fixed phrase in poetry and the novel.
items.cn: unrequited love 在诗歌和小说中成为固定说法。

items.en: The word stays mainly literary, with the love phrase still the most common use.
items.cn: 这个词至今偏文学色彩，搭配 love 的用法仍最常见。

note.en: Unrequited is the negation of requited and belongs with requite, requital, and the language of one-sided feeling.
note.cn: unrequited 是 requited 的否定形式，与 requite、requital 以及「单向情感」的表达相邻。

entries.definition: to give something back for what one has received
entries.definitionCN: 回报；报答

entries.definition: a return or reward for something given
entries.definitionCN: 回报；报偿

entries.definition: returned in kind
entries.definitionCN: 得到回报的

entries.definition: free from noise or movement
entries.definitionCN: 安静的（只是拼写相近，词源不同：源自拉丁语 quietus 的另一个分支）

entries.definition: involving only one person or side
entries.definitionCN: 单方面的

entries.definition: having received no reply
entries.definitionCN: 没有回音的

entries.definition: done without thanks or reward
entries.definitionCN: 费力不讨好的

normalIntro.en: Unrequited is un- plus requited: the giving happened, but nothing is given back.
normalIntro.cn: unrequited 是 un- 加 requited：东西给出去了，却没有回赠。

normal.en: Requite means to give back in return, so unrequited means no return came.
normal.cn: requite 意为回赠报答，所以 unrequited 意为没有回赠。

normal.en: The noun requital is rare but shows the same repayment idea.
normal.cn: 名词 requital 少见，但体现同样的「报答」含义。

normal.en: In modern use the word is almost always tied to love, as in unrequited love.
normal.cn: 在现代用法中，这个词几乎总与爱情相连，如 unrequited love。

normal.en: Compare one-sided: it can describe a match, but unrequited keeps the feeling of a debt unpaid.
normal.cn: 对比 one-sided：后者可描述比赛，而 unrequited 保留了「债没还」的感觉。

normal.en: The opposite is requited, and the verb form would be to requite a love.
normal.cn: 反义形式是 requited，动词形式是 requite a love（回报一份爱）。

abstract.en: Picture a hand holding out a letter over a fence that no one opens.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把信递过篱笆，却没有人来开。

abstract.en: Imagine a coin dropped into a well whose bottom never answers.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚硬币掉进井里，井底始终没有回音。

abstract.en: Think of a song sung to a chair that stays empty in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一首歌唱给角落里那把一直空着的椅子。

examples.en: The novel tells the story of unrequited love across decades.
examples.cn: 这部小说讲述了一段跨越数十年的单相思。

examples.en: Her care for the neighbours stayed unrequited for years.
examples.cn: 她对邻居的关心多年来一直没有得到回报。

examples.en: Poets often turn unrequited longing into their finest lines.
examples.cn: 诗人们常把无回报的思念化作他们最好的诗句。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安瑞快特」——按着「快点回」的意思去期待，结果对方一直不快回，爱就等于没有回应；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: un-（否定）+ requite（回报；古法语 quiter「免除债务」，源自拉丁语 quietus「免除义务的」），字面义「没有被回报的」，核心义「付出却没有回赠」。

sensesIntro.en: Unrequited begins with love that gets no answer and widens to kindness and effort that are never repaid or recognized.
sensesIntro.cn: unrequited 始于得不到回应的爱，再扩展到没有得到回报或认可的好意与努力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand offering flowers over a fence that no one comes to take.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把花递过篱笆，却没人来接。

branches.en: Love without an answer is the dominant sense.
branches.cn: 没有回应的爱是主导义项。

branches.en: Kindness without repayment follows the same pattern.
branches.cn: 没有得到回报的好意沿着同一模式延伸。

branches.en: Effort without recognition is the most general use.
branches.cn: 无人认可的努力是最一般的用法。

branches.en: Poetry keeps the oldest emotional use alive.
branches.cn: 诗歌让最古老的情感用法延续。

branches.en: Both everyday speech and verse describe a gift that never comes back.
branches.cn: 日常说法与诗句都在描述一份始终不回来的馈赠。

intro.en: Unrequited is built from the negative prefix un-, the verb requite, and the past participle ending -ed.
intro.cn: unrequited 由否定前缀 un-、动词 requite 和过去分词词尾 -ed 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin re- means back, and Latin quietus means at rest or free of debt, which Old French quiter turns into to release.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 re- 意为「回」，quietus 意为安宁或免除债务，古法语 quiter 将其发展为「免除」。

items.example: The prefix un- denies that a return happened.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 否定回报的发生。

items.example: The prefix re- supplies the idea of giving back.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 re- 提供「回赠」的意思。

items.example: The ending -ed makes requited a participle.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ed 把 requited 变成分词。

items.example: Requite is the base of the target word.
items.exampleCN: requite 是目标词的词基。

items.example: The noun requital is literary but standard.
items.exampleCN: 名词 requital 偏文学但属标准用法。

items.example: The ending -al forms requital.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -al 构成 requital。

items.example: Requited is the positive of the target word.
items.exampleCN: requited 是目标词的肯定形式。

items.example: The ending -ly can form unrequitedly.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 可构成 unrequitedly。

definition_zh: 不卫生的；有碍健康的；容易致病的
definition_en: not clean and likely to cause disease
core_image: 食物摊旁的下水道敞着口，污水顺着地面流进择菜的篮子
scene: 暴雨过后，后巷的下水口被垃圾堵住，泔水漫到厨房门口。After the storm, the drain in the back lane clogged with rubbish and the kitchen floor became unsanitary.
sceneCN: 这里 unsanitary 是「不卫生的、容易致病的」（第 1 个义项：环境脏乱、有传染疾病的危险）；句意：暴风雨过后，后巷的下水口被垃圾堵住，厨房地面变得不卫生了。

pos.zh: 不卫生的；有碍健康的；容易致病的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加否定前缀的反义参照：去 un- 即「卫生的；有益健康的」
同词根名词：sanitary 去 -ry 加 -tion，义为「环境卫生；卫生设施」
换用拉丁语否定前缀 in- 的英式同义词，义为「不卫生的」
同词根动词：sanitary 加 -ize，义为「消毒；使洁净」

senses.title: Dirty and likely to spread disease
senses.definition: not clean, and therefore likely to cause infection or illness
senses.definitionCN: 不洁净，因此容易引起感染或生病
senses.example: Doctors warned that the camp had unsanitary water supplies.
senses.exampleCN: 医生警告说，营地的供水不卫生。
senses.why: The word is sanitary with the negative prefix, so it names a place that fails the test of health.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 sanitary 加上否定前缀，指的是没通过健康检查的地方。

senses.title: Unhygienic practice
senses.definition: done in a way that breaks hygiene rules, as in cooking or medical care
senses.definitionCN: 以违反卫生规范的方式做事，如做饭或医护
senses.example: Inspectors fined the stall for unsanitary handling of raw meat.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员因该摊位处理生肉不卫生而对其罚款。
senses.why: The adjective can lean on an action as well as a place, because the practice is what creates the health risk.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词既可以修饰地点，也可以修饰动作，因为正是做法造成了健康风险。

senses.title: Filthy in a vivid, everyday way
senses.definition: used emphatically to describe something disgustingly dirty in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 用在日常口语里，强调某物脏得令人反感
senses.example: The shared bathroom was so unsanitary that nobody would use it.
senses.exampleCN: 那间公用浴室脏得没法用，谁都不想进去。
senses.why: Outside official warning, the word works as a strong everyday adjective for a mess you would not touch.
senses.whyCN: 离开正式的警示语境，这个词也常用作很强的日常形容词，形容脏到不想碰的东西。

senses.title: Raising a public health concern
senses.definition: describing conditions that officials or residents regard as a threat to public health
senses.definitionCN: 形容被官员或居民视为公共健康威胁的状况
senses.example: Residents complained that the rubbish dump created unsanitary conditions for the whole district.
senses.exampleCN: 居民抱怨垃圾场给整个街区造成了不卫生的环境。
senses.why: Because the word comes from a public health vocabulary, it naturally carries the tone of a complaint to authorities.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词出自公共卫生用语，天然带有向当局投诉的语气。

intro.en: Unsanitary is a modern English compound: sanitary plus the native negative prefix un-.
intro.cn: unsanitary 是现代英语的合成词：sanitary 加上本族语的否定前缀 un-。

items.en: Sanitas means health, and sanus means healthy.
items.cn: 拉丁语 sanitas 意为健康，sanus 意为健康的。

items.en: Sanitary enters English in the 1840s in the language of public health reform.
items.cn: sanitary 在十九世纪四十年代随公共卫生改革进入英语。

items.en: The prefix un- is the native English negative prefix.
items.cn: 前缀 un- 是英语本族语的否定前缀。

items.en: Unsanitary is formed by adding un- to sanitary during the sanitation debates.
items.cn: 在卫生改革的讨论中，人们把 un- 加到 sanitary 前面构成 unsanitary。

items.en: The word settles into everyday use for drains, kitchens, and crowded housing.
items.cn: 这个词逐渐用于描述下水道、厨房和拥挤的住所，成为日常用词。

note.en: Unsanitary sits next to its positive form sanitary and shares the health field with unclean and unhygienic.
note.cn: unsanitary 与肯定形式 sanitary 相邻，并和 unclean、unhygienic 同属卫生义场。

entries.definition: clean and safe for health
entries.definitionCN: 卫生的；有益健康的

entries.definition: systems for keeping places clean and healthy
entries.definitionCN: 卫生设施；环境卫生

entries.definition: the British variant meaning not sanitary
entries.definitionCN: 英式变体，意思与 unsanitary 相同；这是同义前缀，不是拼写错误

entries.definition: not clean, often with a moral overtone
entries.definitionCN: 不洁净的，常带宗教或道德意味

entries.definition: not done in a healthy and clean way
entries.definitionCN: 不卫生的；不合卫生规范的

entries.definition: covered in dirt and extremely dirty
entries.definitionCN: 污秽的；极脏的

normalIntro.en: Unsanitary is simply sanitary turned negative: take the health tag off a place and it becomes a risk.
normalIntro.cn: unsanitary 就是把 sanitary 变成否定：把「卫生合格」的标签从地方上摘下，它就成了风险。

normal.en: Un- adds not, so unsanitary means not sanitary.
normal.cn: un- 表示「不」，所以 unsanitary 就是 not sanitary（不卫生）。

normal.en: The noun sanitation names the systems that keep a city healthy.
normal.cn: 名词 sanitation 指维持城市健康的卫生系统。

normal.en: Unsanitary conditions are the standard phrase in health reports.
normal.cn: unsanitary conditions 是健康报告里的标准搭配。

normal.en: British writers often prefer insanitary for the same idea.
normal.cn: 英式英语常用 insanitary 表达同样的意思。

normal.en: Compare unclean: unsanitary warns about disease, unclean mainly warns about dirt.
normal.cn: 对比 unclean：unsanitary 强调致病风险，unclean 主要强调脏。

abstract.en: Picture a kitchen where flies walk across the drying plates.
abstract.cn: 想象一间厨房，苍蝇在沥干的盘子上爬来爬去。

abstract.en: Imagine a cook picking up raw chicken with bare hands.
abstract.cn: 想象一位厨师直接用手抓起生鸡肉。

abstract.en: Think of a drain that no one has cleaned for a month.
abstract.cn: 想象一条一个月没人清理过的下水道。

examples.en: The report called the shared kitchen unsanitary and ordered it to be closed.
examples.cn: 报告称这间公用厨房不卫生，并下令将其关闭。

examples.en: Unsanitary conditions in the camp led to a wave of infections.
examples.cn: 营地不卫生的环境引发了一波感染。

examples.en: Food inspectors check whether the stall handles meat in an unsanitary way.
examples.cn: 食品检查员会查看摊位是否以不卫生的方式处理肉类。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安散」——环境安稳、干净，人就不会染病；un 一加，干净被撤走，就变成「不安散」，脏乱易病。这只是拆词联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sanus（健康的）→ sanitas（健康）→ 英语 sanitary（卫生的）；再加本族语否定前缀 un-（不）构成 unsanitary，核心义「失去健康条件」。

sensesIntro.en: Unsanitary starts from the health test, extends to the practices that break it, and then spreads to everyday disgust and public complaint.
sensesIntro.cn: unsanitary 从「健康合格与否」出发，延伸到破坏卫生的做法，再扩展到日常的厌恶感和对公共事务的投诉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: water from an open drain creeping into a food stall.
core.cn: 核心意象：脏水从敞开的下水道漫到食物摊上。

branches.en: A place that fails the health test is the central sense.
branches.cn: 没通过健康检验的地方是核心义项。

branches.en: The same failing applied to an action is the practice sense.
branches.cn: 把同样的不合格用在动作上，就是做法义项。

branches.en: Emotional disgust is the everyday colloquial layer.
branches.cn: 让人恶心的脏是日常口语层面。

branches.en: A threat to a whole district is the public health layer.
branches.cn: 威胁整个街区是公共卫生层面。

branches.en: Both a dirty place and a careless practice add up to the same danger.
branches.cn: 脏乱的地方和马虎的做法，加起来是同样的危险。

intro.en: Unsanitary is built from the negative prefix un- and the Latin-rooted adjective sanitary.
intro.cn: unsanitary 由否定前缀 un- 和拉丁词根的形容词 sanitary 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin sanus means healthy and sanitas means health, the root behind sanitary and sanitation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 sanus 意为健康的，sanitas 意为健康，它们是 sanitary 与 sanitation 的词根。

items.example: Sanus is the root that carries the idea of health.
items.exampleCN: sanus 承载了「健康」这一核心含义。

items.example: Sanitas is the noun form of the same root.
items.exampleCN: sanitas 是同一词根的名词形式。

items.example: Sanitary entered English in the nineteenth century.
items.exampleCN: sanitary 在十九世纪进入英语。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使形容词变成否定。

items.example: The suffix -ary turns sanitas into sanitary.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ary 把 sanitas 变成 sanitary。

items.example: Sanitation is the noun built on the same root.
items.exampleCN: sanitation 是同词根的名词。

items.example: The in- variant is common in British English.
items.exampleCN: in- 变体在英式英语中常见。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ity forms nouns such as sanity.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ity 构成 sanity 等名词。

items.example: Clean is the plain opposite of dirty.
items.exampleCN: clean 是 dirty 的普通反义词。

definition_zh: 不令人满意的；不够好的；不合格的
definition_en: not good enough to meet a need or a standard
core_image: 验收员翻开成绩单，一项一项划过去，最后在末尾打个叉，把本子推回去
scene: 客房的空调修好后又漏了水，前台只回了一句已经登记，房客决定投诉。After the repair failed twice, the tenant called the service unsatisfactory and demanded a refund.
sceneCN: 这里 unsatisfactory 是「不够好的、不合格的」（第 1 个义项：未达到要求或标准）；句意：修了两次都没修好后，租客说这项服务不合格，并要求退款。

pos.zh: 不令人满意的；不够好的；不合格的

derivatives.zh: 基础词加 -ly 构成副词，义为「令人不满地；不合格地」
去掉 un- 的反义参照，义为「令人满意的；合格的」
同词根动词，拉丁语 satis（足够）加 -fy，义为「满足；使满意」
换用 dis- 前缀的同义形容词，义为「不满的」，多修饰人

senses.title: Not meeting a standard
senses.definition: falling below the level that was asked for or required
senses.definitionCN: 低于被要求或规定的水平
senses.example: The examiners graded his work as unsatisfactory.
senses.exampleCN: 考官给他的作业评为不合格。
senses.why: The word negates satisfactory, so it judges a result against a standard and finds the standard unmet.
senses.whyCN: 这个词否定 satisfactory，所以它拿结果与标准对照，结论是标准没达到。

senses.title: Leaving a person unhappy
senses.definition: causing someone to feel that things should have been better
senses.definitionCN: 让人感到本应做得更好
senses.example: Their explanation for the delay was deeply unsatisfactory.
senses.exampleCN: 他们对延误的解释让人非常不满。
senses.why: Satisfy means to fill a need, so something unsatisfactory simply fails to fill it and leaves a gap of mood.
senses.whyCN: satisfy 意为填满需要，所以 unsatisfactory 的东西就是没填满，留下情绪上的缺口。

senses.title: A mild official verdict
senses.definition: used in reports and reviews as a restrained way of saying bad or poor
senses.definitionCN: 在报告和评语中作为「差」的委婉说法
senses.example: The inspectors described the kitchen hygiene as unsatisfactory and set a deadline.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员称厨房卫生不合格，并设定了整改期限。
senses.why: Because it is polysyllabic and formal, it lets an official criticise without using the blunt word bad.
senses.whyCN: 因为它音节多又正式，官员可以借它提出批评，而不必用生硬的 bad 一词。

senses.title: A poor academic mark
senses.definition: in school and university settings, a grade below the passing mark
senses.definitionCN: 在学校场景中指低于及格线的评分
senses.example: She received an unsatisfactory grade and had to retake the module.
senses.exampleCN: 她得了不理想的成绩，不得不重修这门课。
senses.why: Grading is one place where a required level is written down, so the standard sense fits the classroom exactly.
senses.whyCN: 评分场景里有白纸黑字的要求水平，所以「达标与否」这一义项正好贴合课堂。

intro.en: Unsatisfactory is a compound of the native negative prefix un- and the adjective satisfactory, which descends from Latin satis, enough.
intro.cn: unsatisfactory 由本族语否定前缀 un- 和形容词 satisfactory 组成，后者来自拉丁语 satis（足够）。

items.en: Satis means enough, the root of satisfacere, to do enough.
items.cn: 拉丁语 satis 意为足够，是 satisfacere（做够）的词根。

items.en: Satisfacere joins satis with facere, to make, giving the sense of filling a need.
items.cn: satisfacere 把 satis 与 facere（做）结合，表示填满需要。

items.en: Satisfactorius means serving to make amends or to please.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 satisfactorius 意为用于补偿或令人满意的。

items.en: Satisfactory and its noun enter English from Latin forms, with French influence likely.
items.cn: satisfactory 及其名词形式从拉丁语进入英语，也可能经由法语，具体路径存疑。

items.en: The native prefix un- is added to satisfactory; the early spelling is unsatisfactorie.
items.cn: 本族语前缀 un- 加到 satisfactory 前，早期的拼写是 unsatisfactorie；具体首见年代存疑。

items.en: The spelling settles as unsatisfactory and becomes the standard word in reports and grades.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 unsatisfactory，并成为报告与评分中的标准用词。

note.en: Unsatisfactory is the negative partner of satisfactory and sits with inadequate and disappointing in the field of standards.
note.cn: unsatisfactory 是 satisfactory 的否定伙伴，与 inadequate、disappointing 同属「达标与否」的义场。

entries.definition: good enough for a purpose
entries.definitionCN: 令人满意的；达到要求的

entries.definition: displeased, usually describing a person
entries.definitionCN: 不满意的，通常修饰人

entries.definition: the feeling of having what you want
entries.definitionCN: 满足；满意

entries.definition: not enough for what is needed
entries.definitionCN: 不充足的；不够格的

entries.definition: worse than one hoped for
entries.definitionCN: 令人失望的

entries.definition: of a low standard
entries.definitionCN: 差的；质量低的

normalIntro.en: Unsatisfactory is satisfactory with a no attached: the target is set, and the result falls short of it.
normalIntro.cn: unsatisfactory 就是在 satisfactory 前加了一个「不」：目标已经设定，而结果没够到。

normal.en: The stem satisfy carries Latin satis, which means enough.
normal.cn: 词干 satisfy 里有拉丁语 satis，意为「足够」。

normal.en: -fact- comes from facere, to make, so satisfy is to make things enough.
normal.cn: -fact- 来自 facere（做），所以 satisfy 就是「把事做到足够」。

normal.en: -ory turns the verb into an adjective of quality, as in satisfactory.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ory 把动词变成表性质的形容词，如 satisfactory。

normal.en: Un- makes the opposite, so unsatisfactory is not good enough.
normal.cn: un- 表示相反，所以 unsatisfactory 就是「不够好」。

normal.en: Compare dissatisfied: it describes a person, while unsatisfactory describes the thing.
normal.cn: 对比 dissatisfied：它修饰人，而 unsatisfactory 修饰事物。

abstract.en: Picture a marked-up application sheet with a cross at the bottom.
abstract.cn: 想象一张被批改过的申请表，末尾画了个叉。

abstract.en: Imagine a customer holding a receipt and asking for the manager.
abstract.cn: 想象一位顾客拿着收据要找经理。

abstract.en: Think of a half-full cup: not empty, but not enough.
abstract.cn: 想象一只只装了半杯的杯子：不是空的，但也不够。

examples.en: The committee found the manager response unsatisfactory and asked for a full report.
examples.cn: 委员会认为经理的回应令人不满，要求提交完整报告。

examples.en: Her first draft was unsatisfactory, so she rewrote it from the beginning.
examples.cn: 她初稿不合格，于是从头重写了一遍。

examples.en: Unsafe wiring and unsatisfactory hygiene led to the closure of the shop.
examples.cn: 接线不安全加上卫生不合格，导致这家店被关闭。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安满意克特瑞」——想让人「安」心「满意」，结果没做到，就是 unsatisfactory（不满意、不合格）。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 satis（足够）+ facere（做）→ satisfacere（做到足够、使满意）→ 中世纪拉丁语 satisfactorius → 英语 satisfactory（令人满意的）；加否定前缀 un- 得 unsatisfactory，核心义「不够好」。

sensesIntro.en: Unsatisfactory begins with a standard that is not met, then picks up the person left unhappy, and finally hardens into an official or academic verdict.
sensesIntro.cn: unsatisfactory 先指标准没达到，再指被留下的人和情绪，最后固化为官方评语或学业评分。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a form returned with a cross where the mark should be.
core.cn: 核心意象：交回的表单上，本该打分的地方画了个叉。

branches.en: Failing the required level is the central sense.
branches.cn: 未达到要求水平是核心义项。

branches.en: The unhappy reaction of a person is the emotional sense.
branches.cn: 当事人不满的情绪是情感义项。

branches.en: Reports soften bad news with this word as a verdict.
branches.cn: 报告用这个词作为委婉的结论。

branches.en: A grade below the pass mark is the classroom sense.
branches.cn: 低于及格线的评分是课堂义项。

branches.en: All three point at the same line that has not been reached.
branches.cn: 三者都指向同一条没有被够到的线。

intro.en: Unsatisfactory is un- plus satisfactory, and satisfactory itself is built on Latin satis and facere.
intro.cn: unsatisfactory 是 un- 加 satisfactory，而 satisfactory 本身建立在拉丁语 satis 与 facere 上。

latinIntro.en: Latin satis means enough and facere means to make; together they give to satisfy, to make enough.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 satis 意为足够，facere 意为做；两者合起来得出 satisfy，意为「做到足够」。

items.example: Satis supplies the idea of enough.
items.exampleCN: satis 提供「足够」这一核心含义。

items.example: Facere gives the doing part of satisfy.
items.exampleCN: facere 提供 satisfy 中「做」的部分。

items.example: Satisfacere joins both roots into one verb.
items.exampleCN: satisfacere 把两个词根合成一个动词。

items.meaning: relating to, having the quality of
items.example: The suffix -ory forms satisfactory.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ory 构成 satisfactory。

items.example: Satisfactory is the positive base here.
items.exampleCN: satisfactory 是这里的肯定基础词。

items.example: The prefix un- negates the whole adjective.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 使整个形容词变成否定。

items.example: The suffix -ly forms unsatisfactorily.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成 unsatisfactorily。

items.example: The -fac- root also appears in manufacture.
items.exampleCN: 词根 -fac- 也出现在 manufacture 中。

items.example: The dis- prefix marks a negative feeling.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 dis- 标示负面情绪。

items.meaningCN: 表示动作或状态的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -tion forms satisfaction.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -tion 构成 satisfaction。

definition_zh: 不得体的；不合时宜的；有失体面的
definition_en: not suitable or proper for the situation, and likely to offend
core_image: 婚礼席上有人为分钱拍桌争吵，满桌客人默默转开了头
scene: 老人还没下葬，亲戚们已经在客厅里为房产吵成一团。The relatives began to argue about the will at the funeral, which everyone considered unseemly.
sceneCN: 这里 unseemly 是「不得体的、有失体面的」（第 1 个义项：举止在特定场合显得不合适）；句意：亲属们在葬礼上开始为遗嘱争吵，人人都觉得这样有失体统。

pos.zh: 不得体的；不合时宜的；有失体面的

derivatives.zh: 去掉 un- 的反义参照，古旧用法，义为「得体的；适宜的」
同词源基础词，古诺尔斯语意为「适合、相称」，今义为「似乎」
基础词加 -ness 构成名词，义为「不得体；有失体面」
同词源副词：seeming 加 -ly，义为「看似；表面上」，与「相称」的古义已分道

senses.title: Not proper for the occasion
senses.definition: wrong or unsuitable for a particular social situation
senses.definitionCN: 在特定社交场合中不合适、不得当
senses.example: It would be unseemly to laugh at a funeral.
senses.exampleCN: 在葬礼上笑是有失体统的。
senses.why: The root means fitting, so unseemly describes conduct that simply does not fit the setting.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「相称」，所以 unseemly 形容的行为与场合根本不搭。

senses.title: Offending good taste
senses.definition: in poor taste and likely to embarrass or offend others
senses.definitionCN: 品味不佳，容易令人尴尬或反感
senses.example: Guests thought the host unseemly for boasting about the cost.
senses.exampleCN: 客人觉得主人炫耀花费有失体面。
senses.why: Once conduct is judged by a standard of fitting, the same standard easily grows into a judgment of taste.
senses.whyCN: 一旦用「是否相称」来衡量举止，这套标准就会自然扩展成对品味的评判。

senses.title: Improperly keen or fast
senses.definition: used of speed or eagerness that shows the wrong priorities
senses.definitionCN: 形容速度或热切暴露出不恰当的动机
senses.example: Critics attacked the businessman for bidding for the estate with unseemly haste.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者抨击这名商人急不可待地竞购这座宅邸。
senses.why: The word often attaches to haste, because eagerness that arrives too soon betrays what a person really wants.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常搭配「仓促」，因为来得太早的急切会暴露一个人真正的企图。

senses.title: A weakness of public figures
senses.definition: in journalism, behaviour by officials or celebrities that damages their dignity
senses.definitionCN: 新闻语体中指官员或名人有损尊严的行为
senses.example: The minister faced weeks of criticism for his unseemly outburst at a press conference.
senses.exampleCN: 这位部长因在记者会上的失态发火而受到数周批评。
senses.why: Public life sets written and unwritten rules, so the word turns into a fixed label for breaches of decorum.
senses.whyCN: 公共生活有成文与不成文的规矩，这个词于是固化为失礼行为的标签。

intro.en: Unseemly comes from the archaic adjective seemly, itself from the verb seem, which once meant to be fitting, not merely to appear.
intro.cn: unseemly 来自古旧的形容词 seemly，后者出自动词 seem；seem 早年意为「相称」，而不只是「看起来」。

items.en: Sœma means to befit or to honour, the source of the English verb.
items.cn: 古诺尔斯语 sœma 意为「适合、敬重」，是英语动词的来源。

items.en: Seem enters English meaning to be fitting or to suit a person.
items.cn: seem 进入英语时意为「相称、适宜于人」。

items.en: Seemly is formed with the suffix -ly, giving fitting or becoming.
items.cn: seemly 由 seem 加词尾 -ly 构成，表示「合适的、体面的」。

items.en: Un- is prefixed to make unseemly, meaning not fitting.
items.cn: 加否定前缀 un- 构成 unseemly，意为「不相称的」。

items.en: The verb seem narrows to appear, but unseemly keeps the old sense of what does not fit.
items.cn: 动词 seem 后来窄化为「好像」，但 unseemly 仍保留「不合宜」的旧义。

note.en: Unseemly looks like seemly and seems, and sits close to improper and indecorous in the field of conduct.
note.cn: unseemly 与 seemly、seem 形近，并在「举止得体」的义场中与 improper、indecorous 相邻。

entries.definition: proper and fitting, now largely archaic
entries.definitionCN: 得体的；适宜的，现多为古旧用法

entries.definition: the quality of being improper
entries.definitionCN: 不得体；有失体面

entries.definition: to appear to be
entries.definitionCN: 似乎；好像，同源但今义已不同

entries.definition: not correct or acceptable in behaviour
entries.definitionCN: 不合适的；不得体的

entries.definition: lacking good manners or taste
entries.definitionCN: 不得体的；失礼的

entries.definition: seriously offending accepted standards
entries.definitionCN: 有伤风化的；下流的

normalIntro.en: Unseemly is un- plus seemly: seem meant to fit, so unseemly means it does not fit the occasion.
normalIntro.cn: unseemly 是 un- 加 seemly：seem 古义为「相称」，因此 unseemly 就是「与场合不相称」。

normal.en: The verb seem once meant to be fitting, a sense kept only in seemly and unseemly.
normal.cn: 动词 seem 古义为「相称」，只剩在 seemly 与 unseemly 里还保留。

normal.en: Seemly is the positive adjective, and un- flips it to not fitting.
normal.cn: seemly 是肯定形形容词，un- 把它翻转为「不相称」。

normal.en: Unseemly haste is the most common collocation.
normal.cn: unseemly haste（不得体的仓促）是最常见的搭配。

normal.en: The -ly ending here makes an adjective, not an adverb.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ly 构成的是形容词，而非副词。

normal.en: Compare indecent: unseemly is about taste and fit, indecent is about morality.
normal.cn: 对比 indecent：unseemly 关乎品味与合宜，indecent 关乎道德。

abstract.en: Picture a guest shouting at the wedding table while others look away.
abstract.cn: 想象一位客人在婚宴上大声嚷嚷，旁人都转开了眼。

abstract.en: Imagine running to the front of a queue at a memorial service.
abstract.cn: 想象在追悼会上小跑着抢到队伍最前面。

abstract.en: Think of a suit of the wrong size: nothing is broken, it just does not fit.
abstract.cn: 想象一套尺码不对的西装：没坏，只是不合身。

examples.en: There was unseemly haste in selling off the land before the public hearing.
examples.cn: 在公开听证会之前就急着卖地，显得很不合适。

examples.en: The board judged the exchange of gifts unseemly and asked for repayment.
examples.cn: 董事会认为这次赠礼有失体面，要求退回。

examples.en: Some readers disliked the author for showing an unseemly interest in the money side of publishing.
examples.cn: 一些读者不喜欢这位作者对出版业金钱往来表现出的不合宜兴趣。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「俺不稀罕」——在庄重场合大呼「俺不稀罕」地争抢，就显得有失体面，正是 unseemly。这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺尔斯语 sœma（适合、相称）→ 中古英语 seem（相称）→ seemly（得体的）；加否定前缀 un- 得 unseemly（不相称的、不得体的），核心义「与场合不搭」。

sensesIntro.en: Unseemly starts from what does not fit an occasion, then grows into poor taste, haste that reveals motive, and the missteps of public figures.
sensesIntro.cn: unseemly 先指与场合不相称，再扩展为品味不佳、暴露动机的仓促，以及公众人物的失态。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: behaviour that does not fit the room it happens in.
core.cn: 核心意象：举止与所在的房间格格不入。

branches.en: Something that does not fit the occasion is the core sense.
branches.cn: 与场合不相称是核心义项。

branches.en: Judging the behaviour by taste is the social sense.
branches.cn: 用品味评判举止是社交义项。

branches.en: The word clings to haste, where eagerness shows a hidden motive.
branches.cn: 这个词常黏在「仓促」上，急切暴露出隐藏动机。

branches.en: A label for public figures in the press is the journalistic sense.
branches.cn: 新闻中给公众人物贴的标签是新闻语体义项。

branches.en: Both ask whether conduct suits the room and the company.
branches.cn: 两者都在问举止是否配得上场合与在场的人。

intro.en: Unseemly is un- plus seemly, and seemly is built on the Old Norse verb behind seem.
intro.cn: unseemly 是 un- 加 seemly，而 seemly 建立在 seem 背后的古诺尔斯语动词上。

latinIntro.en: The root here is Germanic rather than Latin; the closest Latin idiom is decere, to be fitting, behind decorum.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词根是日耳曼语系的而非拉丁语；最接近的拉丁语表达是 decere（适合），它是 decorum 的来源。

items.example: Sœma is the Norse source of seem.
items.exampleCN: sœma 是 seem 的诺尔斯语来源。

items.meaning: to be fitting, later to appear
items.example: Seem keeps the fitting sense only in seemly.
items.exampleCN: seem 的「相称」义只保留在 seemly 里。

items.meaningCN: 具有……性质的形容词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ly forms seemly, an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ly 构成形容词 seemly。

items.example: Seemly is now archaic outside set phrases.
items.exampleCN: seemly 如今除固定说法外已属古旧用法。

items.example: The prefix un- gives the negative adjective.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 构成否定形容词。

items.meaningCN: 表示状态或性质的名词词尾
items.example: The suffix -ness forms unseemliness.
items.exampleCN: 词尾 -ness 构成 unseemliness。

items.example: Unseemliness names the quality itself.
items.exampleCN: unseemliness 指的是这种性质本身。

items.example: Seemingly follows the newer appear sense of seem.
items.exampleCN: seemingly 走的是 seem 较新的「好像」义。

items.example: Decere is the Latin cousin in meaning, not in root.
items.exampleCN: decere 只在意义上相近，并非同词根。

items.example: Decorum is the quality unseemly behaviour breaks.
items.exampleCN: decorum 正是不得体行为所破坏的东西。

definition_zh: 不支持的；不给予帮助的；不加鼓励的
definition_en: not giving help, encouragement, or approval to someone or something
core_image: 本该递上一只手，手却始终垂在原位没有伸出
scene: 孩子想报考艺术院校，父亲却始终不肯表态支持。Her unsupportive parents refused to attend the exhibition opening.
sceneCN: 这里 unsupportive 是「不给予支持的」（第 1 个义项：不提供帮助与鼓励）；句意：她那对不支持她的父母拒绝出席画展开幕式。

pos.zh: 不支持的；不给予帮助的；不加鼓励的

collocations.zh: 对这项计划不热心支持

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀后的原形，义为「支持的；给予帮助的」
形容词加 -ly 构成，义为「不支持地」
形容词加 -ness 构成，义为「不支持的态度」
整个词族的基础词，义为「支撑；支援」
