senses.title: Failing to give help or encouragement
senses.titleCN: 不给予支持的；不帮忙的
senses.definition: not offering help, encouragement, or emotional backing to another person
senses.definitionCN: 不向他人提供帮助、鼓励或情感上的支持
senses.example: She left the team because the management was unsupportive.
senses.exampleCN: 她离开了那个团队，因为管理层对她不给予支持。
senses.why: The prefix un- negates supportive, so the adjective names the very absence of the helping hand that support implies.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 un- 否定 supportive，于是这个词直接指向「本该伸出的那只手没有伸出」这一缺失状态。

senses.title: Not backing a plan or proposal
senses.definition: not expressing approval of a policy, project, or proposal
senses.definitionCN: 对政策、项目或提案不表示赞同或认可
senses.example: Two board members remained unsupportive of the merger.
senses.exampleCN: 两名董事会成员对合并案始终不表赞同。
senses.why: Support also means to endorse or vote for something, so removing it leaves a stance of open disapproval rather than mere indifference.
senses.whyCN: support 还有「赞成、投票支持」的含义，取消之后剩下的便是一种明确不赞同的立场，而不只是漠不关心。

senses.title: Providing insufficient structural backing
senses.titleCN: 支撑力不足的（引申用法）
senses.definition: used of a structure, system, or argument not strong enough to bear the weight placed on it
senses.definitionCN: 形容结构、体系或论证不够牢固，无法承受所加之重
senses.example: The design was criticised as unsupportive at the joints.
senses.exampleCN: 这个设计被批评为在接合处支撑力不足。
senses.why: The oldest sense of support is to hold something up physically, and this technical use keeps that literal weight-bearing image.
senses.whyCN: support 最古老的义项就是「在物理上撑住」，这条技术用法保留了承重这一最本义的画面。

intro.en: Unsupportive is a modern English construction: the Latin-derived verb support plus the adjectival suffix -ive, then negated by un-.
intro.cn: unsupportive 是近代英语的构词产物：拉丁来源的动词 support 加上形容词后缀 -ive 成为 supportive，再用否定前缀 un- 反转。

items.en: Supportare means to carry or bring up from below, a compound of sub under and portare to carry.
items.cn: 拉丁语 supportare 意为从下方托举、运送，由 sub（在下）与 portare（运送）复合而成。

items.en: Supporter enters French with the sense of bearing or holding up.
items.cn: 古法语 supporter 以「承载、托住」的义项进入法语。

items.en: The verb support appears in English, first of bearing weight and later of backing a person.
items.cn: 动词 support 进入英语，先指承载重量，后来才指支持某人。

items.en: The adjective supportive is formed from support with the suffix -ive.
items.cn: 形容词 supportive 由 support 加后缀 -ive 构成。

items.en: The negated form unsupportive spreads in the nineteenth and twentieth centuries, especially in descriptions of families and workplaces.
items.cn: 否定形式 unsupportive 在十九、二十世纪流行开来，尤其用于描述家庭与职场。

items.en: Today the word is common in psychology, education, and human resources writing.
items.cn: 如今这个词常见于心理学、教育学与人力资源管理文本。

note.en: Unsupportive is the negated form of supportive, so its family members all turn on the Latin image of carrying from below.
note.cn: unsupportive 是 supportive 的否定形式，它整个词族都围绕拉丁语「从下方托举」这一意象展开。

entries.definition: giving help and encouragement
entries.definitionCN: 给予支持与鼓励的（去掉否定前缀的原形）

entries.definition: to hold up or back someone
entries.definitionCN: 支撑；支援

entries.definition: not given help, or not held up by anything
entries.definitionCN: 无人支持的；没有支撑的（后缀不同，重在其结果状态）

entries.definition: not interested or caring either way
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的（强调冷淡，未必有反对之意）

entries.definition: not giving practical help
entries.definitionCN: 不帮忙的；无助于解决问题的

entries.definition: actively unfriendly or opposed
entries.definitionCN: 敌对的；强烈反对的（语气比不表态支持重得多）

normalIntro.en: Unsupportive is simply supportive with the negative un- in front, so it names the missing support rather than open hostility.
normalIntro.cn: unsupportive 就是在 supportive 前加否定前缀 un-，它说的是「支持缺席」，而不是明确的敌意。

normal.en: Unsupportive = un + supportive, so the helping quality is switched off.
normal.cn: unsupportive 就是 un 加 supportive，把「有支持力」这个性质直接关掉。

normal.en: The root portare means to carry, so an unsupportive colleague never takes the weight from you.
normal.cn: 词根 portare 意为「搬运」，所以 unsupportive 的同事从不替你分担重量。

normal.en: People are often unsupportive of a plan they were never invited to shape.
normal.cn: 人们常常不赞成自己没有参与制定的计划。

normal.en: Notice the opposite of unsupportive is supportive, one word, no prefix needed.
normal.cn: 注意 unsupportive 的反面就是 supportive，一个词，不带前缀。

normal.en: In business writing, an unsupportive environment is a polite way to name a discouraging boss or workplace.
normal.cn: 在商务写作里，unsupportive 的环境是一种委婉说法，用来指令人泄气的上司或职场。

abstract.en: Picture a hand already reaching out, then pulled back and kept at the side.
abstract.cn: 想象一只本想伸出的手又缩了回去，一直垂在身体一侧。

abstract.en: Imagine a committee where every vote is a quiet abstention.
abstract.cn: 想象一个委员会，每一次表决都是安静地弃权。

abstract.en: Think of a bridge whose piers stop short of the riverbed.
abstract.cn: 想象一座桥，桥墩还没有触及河床就停住了。

examples.en: Many gifted students give up because the adults around them are unsupportive.
examples.cn: 许多有天赋的学生放弃，是因为身边的大人并不支持他们。

examples.en: Her mentor was never unsupportive, just honest about the risks.
examples.cn: 她的导师从不泼冷水，只是坦率地指出风险。

examples.en: Researchers found that unsupportive leadership increased staff turnover.
examples.cn: 研究者发现，不支持下属的领导方式加剧了员工流失。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「摁着不让走」——想出门求助，却被一只大手摁住肩膀，这就是不给予支持；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 sub（在下）+ portare（运送）→ supportare（托举、承载）→ 英语 support（支撑）→ supportive（支持的）→ un-（不）+ supportive → unsupportive（不支持），核心义「托举的手没有伸出」。

sensesIntro.en: Unsupportive first describes a person who gives no help or encouragement, then a stance against a plan, and finally a technical sense of lacking structural backing.
sensesIntro.cn: unsupportive 先指「不给予帮助与鼓励的人」，再指「对某项计划不表赞同」，最后延伸出「支撑力不足」的技术用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a helping hand that stays at the side instead of reaching out.
core.cn: 核心意象：本该伸出的援手垂在原位没有伸出。

branches.en: No help or encouragement is the everyday personal sense.
branches.cn: 不提供帮助与鼓励是人际关系中的日常义项。

branches.en: Withholding approval of a plan is the institutional sense.
branches.cn: 对提案不表赞同是机构与会议中的义项。

branches.en: Insufficient structural backing is the technical extension.
branches.cn: 结构或论证支撑力不足是技术上的引申义。

branches.en: Both personal neglect and open disapproval signal that the support has been withdrawn.
branches.cn: 个人的冷漠与公开的不赞同，都说明支持已被撤回。

branches.en: A proposal without votes and a structure without piers both rest on nothing.
branches.cn: 没有票数的提案和没有桥墩的建筑，都是悬空的。

intro.en: Unsupportive is built from the prefix un-, the Latin root portare to carry, and the adjectival suffix -ive.
intro.cn: unsupportive 由否定前缀 un-、拉丁词根 portare（运送）与形容词后缀 -ive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supportare combines sub, meaning under, with portare, meaning to carry, and that picture of carrying from below survives in English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 supportare 把 sub（在下）与 portare（运送）组合起来，这种「从下方承托」的画面一直保留到英语里。

items.example: The prefix un- turns supportive into unsupportive.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 supportive 变成 unsupportive。

items.example: The prefix sub- places the support below the weight.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 sub- 把支撑放在重量之下。

items.example: Portare gives the English family port, portable, and transport.
items.exampleCN: portare 衍生出 port、portable 与 transport 等英语词。

items.example: Supportare is the direct source of support.
items.exampleCN: supportare 是 support 的直接来源。

items.example: Support keeps both the physical and the helping senses.
items.exampleCN: support 同时保留物理承托与帮助两层含义。

items.example: The suffix -ive forms supportive from support.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ive 让 support 变成 supportive。

items.example: Supportive describes a person or setting that helps.
items.exampleCN: supportive 描述给予帮助的人或环境。

items.example: Transport shares the carrying root with support.
items.exampleCN: transport 与 support 共享「运送」这一词根。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms unsupportiveness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 unsupportiveness。

latinEntries.meaning: to carry or bring up from below

definition_zh: 不值得信赖的；不可靠的；靠不住的
definition_en: not able to be relied on or believed to keep a promise
core_image: 伸出去的手被人悄悄抽走，握到的只是空气
scene: 室友屡次借钱不还，还总编出新的理由。Most lenders avoid untrustworthy borrowers, however good the sales pitch sounds.
sceneCN: 这里 untrustworthy 是「靠不住的」（第 1 个义项：不能托付信任的人）；句意：无论推销的话说得多么动听，多数放贷方都会避开不可靠的借款人。

pos.zh: 不值得信赖的；不可靠的；靠不住的

derivatives.zh: 去掉否定前缀后的原形，义为「值得信赖的」
名词形式，义为「可靠性；可信度」
否定形式加 -ness 构成，义为「不可靠；不可信」
与 trust 同源、由 dis- 加 -ful 构成的另一支，义为「不信任的」

senses.title: Not safe to trust with a task or promise
senses.definition: not reliable enough to be given a task, a secret, or a promise, because the person is likely to fail you
senses.definitionCN: 不够可靠，不宜托付任务、秘密或承诺，因为对方很可能让你失望
senses.example: After two broken promises, he was seen as untrustworthy.
senses.exampleCN: 两次食言之后，他被人看作靠不住的人。
senses.why: Trust comes from Norse traust, a firmness or shelter, so adding un- and -worthy says the person is not worth resting your weight on.
senses.whyCN: trust 源于古诺斯语 traust，意为「坚固、依托」，加上 un- 与 -worthy 就是说此人撑不起你的分量。

senses.title: Unreliable as a source of information
senses.definition: used of data, evidence, or news that cannot be believed or relied on
senses.definitionCN: 形容数据、证据或新闻无法采信、不能依赖
senses.example: The committee rejected the survey as untrustworthy.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会以不可信为由否决了这项调查。
senses.why: If trust is a shelter, then a report that gives no shelter cannot be the foundation for a decision.
senses.whyCN: 既然 trust 意味着一处可以依靠的庇护所，那么提供不了这种依靠的报告当然不能作为决策的基石。

senses.title: Sly or deceiving in manner appearing
senses.titleCN: 看起来不老实（贬义描述）
senses.definition: describing a look, manner, or behaviour that seems sly or dishonest to an observer
senses.definitionCN: 形容在旁观者眼中显得狡猾、不老实的表情、举止或行为
senses.example: The witness struck the judge as evasive and untrustworthy.
senses.exampleCN: 这名证人在法官眼里显得躲闪而不可信。
senses.why: Judgements of trust pass quickly from concrete promises to the general impression a person gives, and this sense records that leap.
senses.whyCN: 对「可信任」的判断会从具体的承诺迅速滑向一个人给人的整体印象，这条义项记录的正是这一跳跃。

intro.en: Untrustworthy stacks three English pieces: the negative prefix un-, the noun trust from Old Norse, and the adjective suffix -worthy from Old English.
intro.cn: untrustworthy 由三块英语构件叠成：否定前缀 un-、源自古诺斯语的名词 trust，以及源自古英语的形容词后缀 -worthy。

items.en: Traust means trust, help, or firm support, and enters English through northern contact and settlement.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 traust 意为「信任、帮助、坚实的依托」，通过北方人的接触与定居进入英语。

items.en: Weorth means worth or deserving, and the adjective worth emerges from it.
items.cn: 古英语 weorth 意为「价值、值得」，形容词 worth 由此而来。

items.en: Trust is recorded in English with the sense of confidence and reliance on someone.
items.cn: trust 以「信心、对某人的依赖」之义见于英语记录。

items.en: The compound trustworthy, meaning worthy of trust, is formed in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 复合词 trustworthy 意为「值得信任」，形成于十七世纪。

items.en: The negated untrustworthy follows, keeping the same worth and trust pieces.
items.cn: 否定形式 untrustworthy 随之出现，沿用同样的 worth 与 trust 构件。

items.en: In digital life the word now marks fake accounts, unstable links, and doubtful files.
items.cn: 在数字生活中，这个词现在用来标记虚假账号、不稳定的链接与来路可疑的文件。

note.en: Untrustworthy belongs to the trust family, built from trust, worth, and the negating prefix, and it rubs shoulders with words for unreliability.
note.cn: untrustworthy 属于 trust 词族，由 trust、worth 与否定前缀组成，并与一批表示「不可靠」的词相邻。

entries.definition: deserving to be trusted
entries.definitionCN: 值得信赖的（去掉否定前缀的原形）

entries.definition: firm belief that someone is honest
entries.definitionCN: 信任；信赖

entries.definition: too ready to believe other people
entries.definitionCN: 轻信的（注意方向相反：形容信任他人的一方）

entries.definition: cannot be depended on to work or act well
entries.definitionCN: 不可靠的（偏重表现不稳定，未必涉及诚实）

entries.definition: deliberately telling lies
entries.definitionCN: 惯于欺骗的（强调有意说谎）

entries.definition: probably not honest or safe
entries.definitionCN: 可疑的；靠不大住的

normalIntro.en: Untrustworthy is un plus trust plus worthy: literally not worth your trust, so the word says far more than simply unreliable.
normalIntro.cn: untrustworthy 就是 un 加 trust 加 worthy，字面意思是「不值得你信任」，所以它的分量远大于单纯的不可靠。

normal.en: Break it as un + trust + worthy and the meaning is plain: not worth your trust.
normal.cn: 拆成 un + trust + worthy，意思一目了然：不值得你信任。

normal.en: Trust first meant a firm support, so an untrustworthy person is a wall you cannot lean on.
normal.cn: trust 最初指坚固的依托，所以 untrustworthy 的人是一堵你靠不住的墙。

normal.en: Compare untrustworthy with untrusted: the first warns of a character, the second records who has no access.
normal.cn: 对比 untrustworthy 与 untrusted：前者是对品性的警告，后者说明谁没有被授予访问权。

normal.en: Reporters must double-check untrustworthy sources before publishing anything.
normal.cn: 记者在发布任何内容之前都必须反复核对不可信的来源。

normal.en: The -worthy suffix also builds noteworthy, praiseworthy, and trustworthy.
normal.cn: 后缀 -worthy 还能构成 noteworthy、praiseworthy 与 trustworthy 等词。

abstract.en: Picture a handshake where one hand quietly slips free.
abstract.cn: 想象一次握手，其中一只手悄悄抽走了。

abstract.en: Imagine a weather app that says sunny at noon and rains at dusk.
abstract.cn: 想象一个天气应用，中午报晴，傍晚却下雨。

abstract.en: Think of a shopkeeper who smiles while counting your change short.
abstract.cn: 想象一个店主笑着找零，却故意少给你几个硬币。

examples.en: The company was fined for using untrustworthy safety data.
examples.cn: 这家公司因使用不可靠的安全数据而被罚款。

examples.en: She decided that he was untrustworthy with money and kept the accounts herself.
examples.cn: 她认定他在钱财上靠不住，便自己管账。

examples.en: Online shoppers are told to check for untrustworthy links before paying.
examples.cn: 网购者被告知付款前要检查是否有不可信的链接。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安戳丝窝西」——东西一戳就晃、一碰就松，这样的架子谁敢倚靠；纯属谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 古诺斯语 traust（依托、坚固的信任）+ 古英语 weorth（价值、值得）→ 英语 trust（信任）+ -worthy（值得的）→ trustworthy（可信任的）→ un-（不）+ trustworthy → untrustworthy（不值得信任），核心义「靠不住的墙」。

sensesIntro.en: Untrustworthy starts with people you cannot rely on, extends to sources of information that cannot be believed, and ends with an impression of slyness.
sensesIntro.cn: untrustworthy 先指「不能依靠的人」，再扩展到「无法采信的信息来源」，最后落到「显得不老实」的印象判断。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wall you lean on that gives way under your hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：你伸手倚靠的墙在手下松动了。

branches.en: A person who breaks promises is the central personal sense.
branches.cn: 食言、不可托付的人是这个词最核心的人际义。

branches.en: Data and news that mislead form the informational sense.
branches.cn: 误导人的数据与新闻构成信息类义项。

branches.en: An evasive look is the impression-based extension.
branches.cn: 躲闪的神情是基于旁观印象的引申义。

branches.en: Both a broken promise and a shifty glance make an observer stop trusting.
branches.cn: 食言的行为与游移的眼神，都会让旁观者不再信任。

branches.en: A person and a dataset are both untrustworthy when they cannot bear the weight of reliance.
branches.cn: 人和数据集之所以都不可信，都是因为它们承受不住被依赖的重量。

intro.en: Untrustworthy combines the prefix un-, the Norse borrowing trust, and the Old English suffix -worthy.
intro.cn: untrustworthy 组合了前缀 un-、来自古诺斯语的外来词 trust，以及古英语后缀 -worthy。

latinIntro.en: Neither trust nor -worthy is Latin in origin, but the Latin stratum of English supplies the related noun fides, Latin for trust, which feeds confidence, fidelity, and faith.
latinIntro.cn: trust 与 -worthy 都不是拉丁语来源，但英语里的拉丁词汇层提供了对应概念 fides（信任），并由此生出 confidence、fidelity、faith 等词。

items.example: The prefix un- reverses trustworthy.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 un- 把 trustworthy 反转。

items.example: Trust was borrowed from Scandinavian speech.
items.exampleCN: trust 是从斯堪的纳维亚语借来的词。

items.example: The suffix -worthy also builds noteworthy and praiseworthy.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -worthy 还能构成 noteworthy 与 praiseworthy。

items.example: Worthy supplies the value judgement in untrustworthy.
items.exampleCN: worthy 为这个词提供了价值判断的部分。

items.example: Trustworthy is the positive base of the negated form.
items.exampleCN: trustworthy 是否定形式的肯定原形。

items.example: Fides underlies confidence and fidelity.
items.exampleCN: fides 是 confidence 与 fidelity 的词根。

items.example: The suffix -ness forms untrustworthiness.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ness 构成 untrustworthiness。

items.example: Mistrust pairs trust with a different negative prefix.
items.exampleCN: mistrust 用另一个否定前缀与 trust 搭配。

items.example: Distrust carries a stronger note of suspicion.
items.exampleCN: distrust 带有更明显的怀疑意味。

definition_en: to remove a covering from something, or to make a new plan or product publicly known
core_image: 一块垂落的白布被一把扯下，背后的东西第一次露出来
scene: 新品发布会现场灯光暗下，幕布被拉开的瞬间全场安静。The company will unveil its electric lorry at the motor show next week.
sceneCN: 这里 unveil 是「（正式）公布、揭幕」（第 2 个义项：向公众推出新产品或计划）；句意：这家公司将在下周的车展上发布其电动货车。

derivatives.zh: 基础词，义为「面纱；遮盖」
动词加 -ing 构成，义为「揭幕；公布」
动词分词转化为形容词，义为「揭开幕布的；已公布的」
由 veil 加 -ed 构成，义为「蒙着面的；含蓄的」

senses.title: To remove a covering from something
senses.definition: to take away a cloth or other covering so that what is hidden underneath can be seen
senses.definitionCN: 拿开布或其他覆盖物，使被遮住的东西显露出来
senses.example: He unveiled the painting slowly, keeping the crowd waiting.
senses.exampleCN: 他慢慢地揭开油画上的布，让观众一直等着。
senses.why: The word is un- plus veil, so it names the physical act of lifting the veil, its most literal and oldest use.
senses.whyCN: 这个词就是 un 加 veil，指的正是把面纱提起来这个最直接、最古老的动作。

senses.title: To make a new product or plan public
senses.definition: to show or announce something new to the public for the first time, often in a formal event
senses.definitionCN: 首次向公众展示或宣布新事物，常带有正式仪式感
senses.example: The museum unveiled a new education programme in April.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆在四月公布了一项新的教育项目。
senses.why: Once a product is hidden behind the veil of secrecy, showing it is the same gesture moved into business.
senses.whyCN: 一旦新产品被「保密之幕」遮住，把它展示出来就等同于把拉幕的动作搬进商业场合。

senses.title: To formally open a monument
senses.definition: to hold a ceremony in which a statue, plaque, or building is uncovered for the first time
senses.definitionCN: 举行仪式，首次为雕像、铭牌或建筑物揭下覆盖物
senses.example: A war memorial will be unveiled on the hundredth anniversary.
senses.exampleCN: 一座战争纪念馆将在百年纪念日揭幕。
senses.why: Because a veil was once a mark of respect for the dead, unveiling a memorial keeps that ceremonial tone.
senses.whyCN: 面纱在旧时是对逝者的敬意，为纪念物揭幕因此天然带着庄重的仪式色彩。

intro.en: Unveil is a native English compound of un-, the old negative and reversing prefix, and veil, borrowed from Latin velum through French.
intro.cn: unveil 是英语自身构成的复合词：否定兼反转前缀 un- 加上经法语传来的拉丁语 veil（velum）。

items.en: Velum means a sail, curtain, or covering cloth, related to vehere, to carry.
items.cn: 拉丁语 velum 意为「帆、帷幕、遮盖的布」，与 vehere（载运）同源。

items.en: Voile carries the cloth sense into French as a curtain or head covering.
items.cn: 古法语 voile 把「布」的含义带入法语，指帷幕或头巾。

items.en: Veil enters English for the head covering a woman wears, and later for any screen.
items.cn: veil 进入英语，先指女性佩戴的头巾，后来泛指任何遮蔽物。

items.en: The verb unuailen is recorded in the sense of removing a veil or covering.
items.cn: 动词形式在中古英语中已有记录，义为「取下头巾或覆盖物」。

items.en: From the seventeenth century unveil extends to ceremonies that uncover a statue or a building.
items.cn: 自十七世纪起，unveil 扩展到为雕像或建筑揭幕的仪式场合。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word settles into business and media use for launching products and plans.
items.cn: 二十世纪以后，这个词稳定用于商业与媒体语境，指推出新产品与新计划。

note.en: Unveil pairs the reversing prefix un- with veil, and it sits close to verbs of revealing and launching.
note.cn: unveil 由反转前缀 un- 与 veil 组成，在意义上与一组表示「揭示、发布」的动词相邻。

entries.definition: a cloth that covers the face or hides something
entries.definitionCN: 面纱；遮蔽物（unveil 的基础词）

entries.definition: covered or expressed in an indirect way
entries.definitionCN: 蒙着面的；含蓄的（与 unveil 状态相反）

entries.definition: not able to be obtained
entries.definitionCN: 无法获取的（只是拼写相近，词源不同，from avail）

entries.definition: to make something known or visible
entries.definitionCN: 揭示；透露（适用范围比 unveil 更广）

entries.definition: to bring a new product to the market
entries.definitionCN: 推出；上市（偏重上市与投放市场）

entries.definition: to remove a cover from something
entries.definitionCN: 揭开覆盖物；揭露

normalIntro.en: Unveil is literally to un-veil, to take the veil off, so the physical lifting of a cloth stands behind every figurative sense.
normalIntro.cn: unveil 字面就是「去掉面纱」，把布掀开的动作藏在它每一个比喻义背后。

normal.en: Unveil = un + veil, so it simply means take the veil off.
normal.cn: unveil 就是 un 加 veil，意思就是「把面纱取下来」。

normal.en: The prefix un- here reverses an action rather than forming a pure negative.
normal.cn: 这里的前缀 un- 是撤销动作，而不只是单纯的否定。

normal.en: Veil comes from Latin velum, a piece of cloth, related to words for carrying and sailing.
normal.cn: veil 来自拉丁语 velum（一块布），与表示「运送、航行」的词同源。

normal.en: Companies unveil products, museums unveil programmes, and cities unveil statues.
normal.cn: 公司发布产品，博物馆公布项目，城市为雕像揭幕。

normal.en: The past participle unveiled works as an adjective: an unveiled statue, an unveiled plan.
normal.cn: 过去分词 unveiled 可作形容词：揭幕后的雕像、已公布的计划。

abstract.en: Picture a white sheet sliding off a sculpture as a crowd gasps.
abstract.cn: 想象白布从雕像上滑落，人群发出一声惊叹。

abstract.en: Imagine a phone still in a black cloth bag on a stage before the countdown.
abstract.cn: 想象倒计时之前，舞台上的黑布袋里还裹着一部手机。

abstract.en: Think of a plaque that has been covered since the day it was made, waiting for its ceremony.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从制成那天起就被盖住的铭牌，一直等待自己的仪式。

examples.en: The mayor will unveil a plaque in honour of the old theatre.
examples.cn: 市长将为这座老剧院揭幕一块纪念铭牌。

examples.en: The team unveiled its new kit on social media yesterday.
examples.cn: 球队昨天在社交媒体上发布了新款球衣。

examples.en: Engineers unveiled a bridge design that could survive strong floods.
examples.cn: 工程师们公布了一项能抵御强洪水的桥梁设计。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「安围」——先安安稳稳地围上一层布，再把布一扯，就是揭开；这是拆分联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 velum（帆、幕布）→ 古法语 voile → 英语 veil（面纱、遮盖物）→ un-（除去）+ veil → unveil（揭开；公布），核心义「扯下遮布，让里面的东西现身」。

sensesIntro.en: Unveil moves from the literal lifting of a cloth, through the public launch of a product or plan, to the ceremony that opens a monument.
sensesIntro.cn: unveil 从「揭开布」这一具体动作出发，延伸到「公布新产品或计划」，再到「为纪念物举行揭幕仪式」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a white cloth pulled away to show what it covered.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块白布被扯下，露出被遮住的东西。

branches.en: Lifting a covering is the literal sense.
branches.cn: 揭开覆盖物是最直接的本义。

branches.en: Making a new product public is the media and business sense.
branches.cn: 向公众推出新产品是媒体与商务义项。

branches.en: A formal opening ceremony for a monument is the commemorative sense.
branches.cn: 为纪念物举行的揭幕仪式是纪念性义项。

branches.en: Both a picture being uncovered and a statue being inaugurated use the same gesture.
branches.cn: 揭开一幅画与为雕像揭牌，用的是同一个手势。

branches.en: A launch event and a memorial ceremony both stage the moment of revelation in public.
branches.cn: 发布会与纪念仪式都把「揭示」的那一刻摆到公众面前。

intro.en: Unveil is built from the reversing prefix un- and the Latin-derived noun and verb veil.
intro.cn: unveil 由表示撤销的前缀 un- 与拉丁来源的名词、动词 veil 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin velum, a cloth or sail, gives English veil, and the Latin verb revelare gives reveal, its near twin.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 velum（布、帆）给英语带来 veil，拉丁动词 revelare 则带来与它意义相近的 reveal。

items.example: The prefix un- in unveil undoes the covering.
items.exampleCN: unveil 中的 un- 撤销了遮盖的动作。

items.example: Velum provides the cloth image in veil.
items.exampleCN: velum 为 veil 提供了「布」的意象。

items.example: Veil entered English through Old French voile.
items.exampleCN: veil 经古法语 voile 进入英语。

items.example: A veiled threat keeps the meaning behind a cover.
items.exampleCN: 含蓄的威胁把意思藏在遮盖之后。

items.example: The unveiled portrait hung above the fireplace.
items.exampleCN: 揭幕后的肖像挂在壁炉上方。

items.example: Revelare gives English reveal.
items.exampleCN: revelare 衍生出英语 reveal。

items.meaning: to open up and make known
items.example: Disclose is a formal cousin of unveil.
items.exampleCN: disclose 是 unveil 较正式的同类词。

items.example: The suffix -ing forms the noun unveiling.
items.exampleCN: 后缀 -ing 构成名词 unveiling。

items.example: Velifer shows the sail sense of velum.
items.exampleCN: velifer 体现了 velum 的「帆」义。
